blackbox.does: Selects the highest mutually supported API version from the client-accepted set and the server-offered set, or reports that no compatible version exists.

problem_solution.problem: Clients and servers support overlapping but different API versions, and mismatched assumptions cause silent breakage when neither side negotiates explicitly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes a single version and fails opaquely when the server no longer offers it, with no fallback to a compatible version.
problem_solution.solution: A negotiator that intersects the accepted and offered version sets and picks the best common version or returns an explicit incompatibility.
known_pitfalls: hard-coding a version with no fallback
picking a version outside the offered set
no clear signal when nothing is compatible
success_signals: a compatible version is chosen when one exists
incompatibility is reported explicitly

blackbox.does: Dispatches a batch of independent API requests with bounded concurrency and aggregates their results, keeping per-request outcomes so partial failures are visible.

problem_solution.problem: Making many independent API calls one at a time is slow, while firing them all at once overwhelms the upstream and loses track of which failed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent either loops sequentially or launches unbounded concurrent calls that trip rate limits and collapse all failures into one error.
problem_solution.solution: A fanout that runs the batch with a bounded concurrency limit and returns per-request outcomes so partial failures are attributable.
known_pitfalls: collapsing distinct failures into one error
losing the mapping from request to result
success_signals: concurrency stays within the limit
per-request success and failure is preserved

blackbox.does: Derives a suite of request and response contract tests from an API specification so that any drift between the implementation and the declared contract is caught.

problem_solution.problem: Implementations drift from their published API contract over time, and manual contract tests are incomplete and go stale.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a couple of happy-path tests that miss required fields, error responses, and status codes, so drift goes undetected.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that turns the spec into contract tests covering each operation's request schema, response schema, and declared status codes.
known_pitfalls: tests that go stale when the spec changes
success_signals: tests fail when the implementation drifts
each operation and error response is covered

blackbox.does: Sends a conditional request with the stored entity validator and returns the cached representation unchanged on a not-modified response, refreshing it only when the resource changed.

problem_solution.problem: Polling an endpoint re-downloads the full body every time even when nothing changed, wasting bandwidth and quota.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent always does an unconditional GET and re-processes an identical body, never sending the stored validator.
problem_solution.solution: A conditional fetcher that sends the stored entity tag and treats a not-modified response as a cache hit, refetching only on change.
known_pitfalls: caching a representation past its validity
success_signals: unchanged resources return from cache
the body is refetched only on change

blackbox.does: Resolves a GraphQL field for its declared type by loading the requested data, honoring the selection set, and returning a result that matches the schema type for that field.

problem_solution.problem: GraphQL resolvers commonly reload the same related records per parent, and a resolver that returns a shape off the schema type breaks the whole query.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a resolver that queries per item in a list, producing an N+1 explosion, and returns fields the schema type does not declare.
problem_solution.solution: A resolver skeleton that batches related loads, respects the selection set, and returns exactly the schema-typed shape for the field.
known_pitfalls: returning fields off the schema type
ignoring null and error propagation rules
success_signals: results match the schema type
related records load in batches

blackbox.does: Handles a unary gRPC method by decoding the request against its protobuf contract, invoking the handler, and encoding a response with the declared status semantics.

problem_solution.problem: gRPC handlers must honor the protobuf message contract and status-code conventions, and hand-written glue often maps errors to the wrong status.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns a generic error for every failure and ignores the declared status codes, so clients cannot distinguish retryable from terminal errors.
problem_solution.solution: A wrapper that decodes and encodes against the proto contract and maps handler outcomes onto the correct gRPC status semantics.
known_pitfalls: mapping all errors to a single status
field-number drift between client and server protos
success_signals: responses conform to the proto contract
status codes distinguish error classes

blackbox.does: Generates a runnable mock server from an API specification that returns schema-valid example responses per operation so clients can be developed before the real API exists.

problem_solution.problem: Client teams are blocked waiting for a backend to exist, and ad hoc stubs drift from the actual API contract.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-writes stub responses that do not match the spec schema, so client code passes against the stub but fails against the real API.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that reads the API spec and emits a mock server returning schema-valid examples for each declared operation.
known_pitfalls: responses that violate the declared schema
success_signals: mock responses validate against the spec
every operation is represented

blackbox.does: Binds a described OpenAPI operation to a typed call that validates arguments against the operation schema, issues the request, and returns a validated typed response.

problem_solution.problem: Hand-written HTTP calls against a documented API drift from the spec, sending wrong parameter names and mis-parsing responses that later change shape.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds URLs and payloads by hand from memory, omitting required parameters and ignoring the declared response schema.
problem_solution.solution: A wrapper that derives the request and response contract from the OpenAPI operation, validating both sides against the spec.
known_pitfalls: not surfacing the documented error responses
success_signals: requests conform to the operation contract
responses are validated against the spec

blackbox.does: Checks an OpenAPI document against structural validity and a style ruleset, reporting each finding with its location and severity so specs stay consistent and valid.

problem_solution.problem: OpenAPI documents accumulate structural errors and inconsistent conventions that break code generation and confuse consumers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent edits the spec by hand and introduces invalid references or inconsistent naming that only surface when generation later fails.
problem_solution.solution: A linter that validates the document structure and applies a shared style ruleset, emitting located, severity-ranked findings.
known_pitfalls: treating warnings and errors the same
success_signals: invalid documents are flagged with locations
style deviations are reported consistently

blackbox.does: Walks a paginated endpoint by following its cursor or link metadata and yields a single continuous stream of records with a bounded page budget and loop protection.

problem_solution.problem: Callers frequently read only the first page of a paginated API and miss the rest, or loop forever when a cursor never terminates.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent fetches one page and treats it as the full result, or follows next-cursors with no page cap and spins indefinitely on a broken cursor.
problem_solution.solution: An expander that follows the documented pagination metadata to completion with a page budget and repeat-cursor detection.
known_pitfalls: infinite loops on a stuck cursor
success_signals: all pages traversed to completion
no infinite loop on a broken cursor

blackbox.does: Issues a request while reading rate-limit headers, pacing calls under the remaining budget and honoring retry-after guidance on throttling responses before retrying.

problem_solution.problem: Clients ignore published rate-limit headers and get throttled or banned, then retry immediately and make the throttling worse.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent retries a 429 in a tight loop with no delay, ignoring the retry-after header and burning the remaining quota faster.
problem_solution.solution: A fetcher that reads the remaining-quota and retry-after headers, paces requests under budget, and waits the advised interval before retrying.
known_pitfalls: sharing no budget state across concurrent callers
success_signals: requests stay within the published budget
throttling responses are honored before retry

blackbox.does: Maps varied upstream API responses and error shapes onto one standard result-and-error envelope so downstream callers handle success and failure uniformly.

problem_solution.problem: Integrating several upstream APIs means each returns success and errors in its own shape, forcing callers to branch on vendor-specific structures.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sprinkles per-vendor response parsing across call sites, so adding an upstream means touching every consumer.
problem_solution.solution: A normalizer that folds each upstream shape into a single result-or-error envelope with a consistent error taxonomy.
known_pitfalls: losing upstream error detail in the mapping
success_signals: callers handle one envelope shape
upstream error detail is preserved in the taxonomy

blackbox.does: Materializes the standard collection and item routes for a resource with consistent verbs, status codes, and error envelopes derived from the resource specification.

problem_solution.problem: Every resource re-implements list, read, create, update, and delete with subtly different status codes, pagination, and error shapes across a service.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes each endpoint from scratch, returning 200 for creates, inconsistent error bodies, and missing not-found handling.
problem_solution.solution: A resource-group generator that emits the standard routes from a spec with uniform verbs, status codes, and a shared error envelope.
known_pitfalls: missing not-found and validation error handling
success_signals: routes follow uniform conventions
error envelopes are consistent across resources

blackbox.does: Wraps an injected SDK method call and emits a structured receipt capturing the method, redacted arguments, outcome status, and timing without altering the call result.

problem_solution.problem: Third-party SDK calls are opaque, so failures and slow calls are hard to attribute and audit after the fact.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent calls the SDK directly with no record, so when a call fails intermittently there is no trace of arguments, timing, or outcome.
problem_solution.solution: A pass-through wrapper that records a structured, redacted receipt around each SDK call while returning the original result unchanged.
success_signals: every call has an auditable receipt
sensitive arguments are redacted
the result is unchanged

blackbox.does: Flattens a stream of API response pages into a single normalized record set, extracting the records array per a declared path.

problem_solution.problem: API pages wrap records in envelopes; downstream code wants a flat, typed record set.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Keeps the page envelopes or loses records nested under a data key.
problem_solution.solution: A flatten primitive that extracts the records path and concatenates into one set.
success_signals: record count equals sum of pages
flat set

blackbox.does: Maps a raw API response to a target record schema with field renames, type coercion, and defaults, quarantining rows that fail.

problem_solution.problem: Each API returns a different shape; downstream needs one canonical schema with bad rows isolated.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Passes raw nested API JSON downstream, breaking every consumer.
problem_solution.solution: A normalize primitive mapping to a target schema with coercion, defaults, and a quarantine.
success_signals: output matches target schema
bad rows quarantined not dropped

blackbox.does: Exchanges client credentials for a scoped access token, caching until expiry and never logging the secret.

problem_solution.problem: Every API integration re-implements token exchange, caching, and refresh, often leaking secrets in logs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Requests a new token on every call and prints the secret while debugging.
problem_solution.solution: A token primitive that caches until expiry, refreshes, and redacts the secret.
success_signals: token cached until expiry
no secret in logs

blackbox.does: Fetches all pages of an API endpoint following the declared pagination style (page/offset/cursor/link), honoring rate limits and retries.

problem_solution.problem: Pulling a full dataset from an API means correct pagination, rate-limit backoff, and partial-failure handling every time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Fetches only the first page or hammers the API past its rate limit.
problem_solution.solution: A pagination primitive that walks all pages per the declared style with backoff and a receipt.
success_signals: all pages retrieved
no page skipped or duplicated

blackbox.does: Provisions a new user identity record from a validated signup, assigning a stable account identifier and initial status, and rejects duplicates atomically.

problem_solution.problem: Creating the durable identity record is where race conditions produce duplicate accounts and partially provisioned users.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent issues a check-then-insert without a unique constraint or transaction, creating duplicate or orphaned accounts under concurrency.
problem_solution.solution: An atomic provisioning capability that enforces uniqueness at write time and emits a stable account id with an initial lifecycle state.
known_pitfalls: storing raw secrets alongside the record
success_signals: exactly one record per identity under load
stable id returned
duplicate attempts rejected cleanly

blackbox.does: Transitions an account to an inactive state that blocks authentication while preserving the record, and revokes active sessions for the subject.

problem_solution.problem: Deactivation is often conflated with deletion or leaves active sessions alive so a disabled account can still act.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flips an active flag but leaves refresh tokens valid and login paths that skip the status check, so the account still works.
problem_solution.solution: A reversible capability that marks the account inactive, enforces the status check on all auth paths, and revokes existing sessions.
success_signals: inactive account cannot authenticate
sessions revoked
state is reversible

blackbox.does: Records a verified account deletion request, schedules the irreversible erasure workflow after any grace period, and acknowledges the request to the subject.

problem_solution.problem: Deletion requests must be verified, honored within a policy window, and coordinated across services, yet are often lost or silently ignored.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes one table row immediately with no verification or grace period, breaking references and losing audit and reversal ability.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that verifies intent, opens a tracked deletion ticket with a grace window, and hands off to the downstream erasure workflow.
known_pitfalls: losing the audit trail of the request
success_signals: request verified and ticketed
grace window honored
downstream erasure scheduled

blackbox.does: Validates a presented email verification token against the stored single-use challenge and, on success, marks the address confirmed and consumes the token.

problem_solution.problem: Confirmation endpoints often accept expired or already-used tokens and fail to bind the token to the right account.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares tokens with a non-constant-time check, ignores expiry, and lets a token be replayed to confirm repeatedly.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that verifies the hashed token in constant time, enforces expiry and single use, and flips the confirmed flag exactly once.
success_signals: expired or used tokens rejected
confirmation is idempotent
address marked verified once

blackbox.does: Mints a single-use, time-bounded email verification token for an account and dispatches it to the registered address without exposing the raw token server-side.

problem_solution.problem: Email confirmation links are frequently long-lived, reusable, or guessable, turning them into an account-takeover vector.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent emails a raw sequential id or a token with no expiry and stores it in plaintext, so links never expire and are enumerable.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that issues a high-entropy, hashed, single-use token with an explicit expiry and dispatches only the opaque value by email.
success_signals: tokens are single-use and expire
only the hash is stored
dispatch is recorded

blackbox.does: Invalidates every active session and refresh handle for a subject in one operation so all devices are signed out simultaneously.

problem_solution.problem: After a credential compromise users need to terminate all sessions, but systems often can only end the current one.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent only clears the current cookie and leaves refresh tokens on other devices alive, so the attacker keeps access.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that bumps a per-subject session epoch or enumerates and revokes all active handles, invalidating every device at once.
known_pitfalls: missing refresh tokens on other devices
success_signals: all devices require re-authentication
concurrent refresh is defeated
operation is idempotent

blackbox.does: Verifies a presented second-factor proof against the enrolled factor within its validity window and marks the proof consumed to block replay.

problem_solution.problem: Second-factor verification often accepts codes outside their window or allows the same code to be replayed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks a one-time code with no drift bound and no used-code tracking, so a captured code can be replayed within its lifetime.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that validates the proof within a bounded skew window and records each accepted proof as consumed to prevent replay and brute force.
success_signals: out-of-window proofs rejected
each code accepted at most once
brute force is throttled

blackbox.does: Registers an additional authentication factor for a subject, provisioning the factor material and confirming it with a proof before activation.

problem_solution.problem: MFA enrollment can activate a factor without proving the user actually controls it, or store the factor secret in the clear.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent turns on a factor immediately from a generated secret without a confirming code and saves the secret unencrypted next to the account.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that provisions the factor, requires a valid confirmation proof before activation, and stores factor material protected at rest.
known_pitfalls: binding factor to the wrong subject
success_signals: factor active only after proof
secret protected at rest
recovery path provided

blackbox.does: Performs a server-to-server exchange with an authorization server to obtain or exchange tokens for a grant, authenticating the client and honoring returned scopes and lifetimes.

problem_solution.problem: Token endpoint calls often mishandle client authentication, scope downgrades, and secure storage of the returned tokens.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent puts the client secret in a query string, ignores the returned scope, and caches tokens past their expiry in plaintext.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that authenticates the client correctly, requests only needed scopes, and stores the returned tokens protected with their real lifetimes.
known_pitfalls: client secret in URL or logs
no retry or error handling on the token endpoint
success_signals: client authenticated per provider spec
only needed scopes requested
tokens stored with real expiry

blackbox.does: Handles the redirect from an OpenID provider, validating state and PKCE, exchanging the code, and verifying the returned identity token before establishing a local identity.

problem_solution.problem: OIDC callbacks are commonly implemented without state, nonce, or issuer and audience checks, opening CSRF and token-substitution attacks.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts the returned id token without verifying signature, issuer, audience, nonce, or expiry and skips the state and PKCE checks.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that validates the state and PKCE verifier, exchanges the code at the token endpoint, and fully verifies the id token claims before trusting it.
core_components: id token signature and claim verification
success_signals: state and nonce validated
id token fully verified before use
replayed codes rejected

blackbox.does: Verifies a presented identifier and password against the stored credential and returns an allow or deny decision with generic failure messaging.

problem_solution.problem: Login verification leaks account existence through differential responses and timing, and often skips slow-hash comparison.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns different errors for unknown user versus wrong password and short-circuits hashing when the user is missing, enabling enumeration.
problem_solution.solution: A verifier that performs a slow-hash comparison on a uniform code path and returns a single generic failure regardless of which factor was wrong.
success_signals: identical response for unknown user and bad password
constant-time behavior
no secret in logs

blackbox.does: Validates a reset token and applies a new password that meets policy, atomically consuming the token and invalidating existing sessions on success.

problem_solution.problem: Reset confirmation often forgets to expire the token, enforce password policy, or revoke sessions after a change.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent updates the password but leaves the reset token reusable and keeps old sessions alive, so a prior attacker session persists.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that verifies the hashed token once, enforces the new-password policy, updates the credential, and revokes existing sessions atomically.
success_signals: token consumed on first use
new password meets policy
all prior sessions invalidated

blackbox.does: Accepts a password reset request for an identifier and, when it maps to an account, issues a single-use time-bounded reset token by the registered channel.

problem_solution.problem: Reset request endpoints leak which accounts exist and issue guessable or long-lived reset tokens.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent replies success only when the account exists and mints a plaintext token with no expiry, enabling enumeration and takeover.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that responds uniformly regardless of account existence and, when applicable, issues a hashed single-use short-lived token out of band.
known_pitfalls: token sent to changeable contact without checks
success_signals: identical response whether or not the account exists
tokens single-use and short-lived
requests are rate limited

blackbox.does: Applies a validated partial update to a subject profile, enforcing which fields are self-editable and re-verifying security-sensitive fields before they change.

problem_solution.problem: Profile update endpoints frequently allow mass assignment of privileged fields and change email or phone without re-verification.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent binds the whole request body onto the record, letting a user set role or verified flags and swap contact fields without proof.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that whitelists self-editable fields, rejects privileged mutations, and routes security-sensitive changes through re-verification.
known_pitfalls: mass assignment of role or flags
changing email or phone without re-verification
success_signals: only allowed fields change
privileged mutations rejected
sensitive changes require re-verification

blackbox.does: Checks a signup submission against structural, format, and policy rules and reports each field-level violation without creating any account.

problem_solution.problem: Every product reinvents signup validation and drifts between client and server rules, letting malformed or duplicate registrations through.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-codes ad hoc regex checks that miss password policy, unicode edge cases, and uniqueness, then trusts client-side validation.
problem_solution.solution: A single server-side validator that applies the shared signup policy and returns structured, field-addressed verdicts.
known_pitfalls: leaking whether an email already exists
success_signals: invalid payloads rejected with clear field errors
valid payloads normalized consistently
no account side effects on failure

blackbox.does: Establishes an authenticated session for a subject, minting bound access and refresh material with explicit lifetimes and device binding metadata.

problem_solution.problem: Session establishment is where fixation, unbounded lifetimes, and unbound tokens create long-lived hijack opportunities.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reuses a pre-auth session id, sets no expiry, and issues tokens with no audience or device binding, enabling fixation and replay.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that mints a fresh, bound session with separate short-lived access and rotating refresh material and explicit lifetimes.
success_signals: new id on every login
bounded lifetimes enforced
access and refresh bound to context

blackbox.does: Exchanges a valid refresh handle for renewed session material, rotating the refresh secret and detecting reuse of a previously rotated handle.

problem_solution.problem: Refresh tokens that are not rotated or reuse-detected let a single stolen token grant indefinite access.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps the same refresh token across renewals and never invalidates the old one, so a leaked token works forever undetected.
problem_solution.solution: A rotation capability that issues a new refresh secret on each use, invalidates the prior one, and revokes the family on reuse detection.
success_signals: old refresh handle invalidated on use
reuse triggers family revocation
renewals are auditable

blackbox.does: Invalidates a specific session or token so that subsequent presentations are rejected, and records the revocation for audit.

problem_solution.problem: Stateless tokens are hard to revoke, so compromised sessions often remain valid until their natural expiry.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent relies solely on token expiry and provides no revocation path, leaving stolen tokens usable until they age out.
problem_solution.solution: A revocation capability that records an invalidation marker checked on every presentation, taking effect immediately and idempotently.
known_pitfalls: no server-side revocation for stateless tokens
revocation not checked on read path
success_signals: revoked token rejected immediately
repeat revoke is a no-op
revocation is logged

blackbox.does: Derives an admin data-table specification from a resource schema, choosing columns, filters, sort options, and row actions consistent with the declared field types.

problem_solution.problem: Every admin dashboard needs list tables per resource, and hand-writing column, filter, and action config for each entity is repetitive and drifts from the schema.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-codes a bespoke table per model, omitting sort or filter config and letting the columns fall out of sync with the schema over time.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that reads the resource schema and emits a declarative admin-table spec with columns, filters, sort options, and row actions.
known_pitfalls: sensitive fields exposed as default columns
unsortable or unfilterable types offered as options
success_signals: generated spec matches golden output for a fixture schema
sensitive fields excluded unless explicitly allowed

blackbox.does: Moves a record between active and archived states under a retention policy and restores it on request, preserving its identity and relationships across the transition.

problem_solution.problem: Long-lived data apps need to retire records from the working set without losing them, and to bring them back cleanly, without breaking references either way.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies a record to an archive table and deletes the original, breaking foreign keys and making restore reassign a new identifier.
problem_solution.solution: An archive-restore capability that flips an archive state under a retention policy, preserving identity and relationships so restore is a clean inverse.
known_pitfalls: references broken by moving rows between tables
archived records still counted in active metrics
success_signals: archive then restore returns an equivalent record
relationships remain valid across both directions

blackbox.does: Appends a tamper-evident audit entry recording who did what to which resource and when, to an append-only trail that later reads and reviews depend on.

problem_solution.problem: Compliance and forensics need an immutable record of who changed what and when, but ad hoc log lines are mutable, unstructured, and easy to lose.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes free-text log lines that can be edited or dropped and omit the actor or target, so the trail is not defensible.
problem_solution.solution: An audit capability that appends a structured, append-only entry with actor, action, target, and timestamp, keyed so duplicates are suppressed.
success_signals: entries are append-only and never updated in place
retried writes collapse to a single entry

blackbox.does: Validates a batch of candidate rows against schema, type, and referential rules and returns per-row accept or reject results without writing any records.

problem_solution.problem: Bulk imports fail late and partially when rows are only checked as they are inserted, leaving the store half-written and the operator without a clear reject list.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent streams rows straight into inserts and stops at the first bad row, leaving the import half-applied with no report of what failed.
problem_solution.solution: A validation-only capability that checks every candidate row against schema, type, and referential rules up front and returns a per-row accept/reject report.
known_pitfalls: silent type coercion masking bad data
success_signals: every row labeled accept or reject with a reason
no records written during validation

blackbox.does: Returns a cached value for a key or computes it once on a miss, stores it under a time-to-live, and coordinates concurrent misses to avoid redundant fills.

problem_solution.problem: Read-through caches must serve hits, fill misses exactly once, and expire entries, or concurrent misses stampede the source and stale values linger.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent caches without a time-to-live or miss coordination, so entries never expire and a burst of misses recomputes the same value in parallel.
problem_solution.solution: A get-or-fill capability that serves cache hits, computes a miss once behind a guard, stores under a time-to-live, and returns the value with its cache status.
known_pitfalls: entries with no expiry serving stale data
caching error or empty results as if valid
success_signals: a miss computes the value once under contention
expired keys are recomputed on next access

blackbox.does: Produces a create-and-edit form specification from a resource schema, mapping field types to inputs and carrying validation rules and default values.

problem_solution.problem: Create and edit forms must mirror the resource schema and its validation, and rebuilding them per entity duplicates field-to-input mapping and validation wiring.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a fixed form and forgets required-field markers or validation, so the form accepts input the backend then rejects.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that maps schema field types to form inputs, attaches validation rules and defaults, and emits a declarative form spec for create and edit.
known_pitfalls: client validation diverging from the schema
required fields not marked in the form
unsupported field types rendered as raw text
success_signals: form validation mirrors the backend schema
generated spec matches golden output for a fixture schema

blackbox.does: Serializes a filtered set of records into a downloadable file in a requested format, applying field redaction and a row bound according to the export policy.

problem_solution.problem: Exports must render records to a chosen format with consistent field selection and redaction, or they leak sensitive columns and produce files that fail to round-trip.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent dumps every column to CSV with no redaction or row bound, leaking private fields and producing an unbounded file.
problem_solution.solution: An export capability that selects and redacts fields per policy, bounds the row set, and emits a well-formed file in the requested format.
known_pitfalls: leaking sensitive columns in the export
delimiter or encoding breaking the file
success_signals: exported file re-parses to the selected fields
redacted fields absent from the output

blackbox.does: Returns a bounded page of resources matching a whitelist of filters in a requested sort order, with a stable total-or-cursor summary for the result set.

problem_solution.problem: Listing endpoints must filter and sort on allowed fields only and always bound the result, or they invite unbounded scans and injection via arbitrary sort keys.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent interpolates client-supplied filter and sort fields directly and returns the whole table, enabling injection and unbounded responses.
problem_solution.solution: A list capability with a filter and sort whitelist, an enforced page bound, and a deterministic order for stable pagination.
known_pitfalls: sort or filter injection via arbitrary fields
success_signals: only whitelisted fields accepted for filter and sort
page size never exceeds the enforced bound

blackbox.does: Serves a stable slice of an ordered result set from an opaque cursor and returns the next cursor, so callers can traverse large collections without drift.

problem_solution.problem: Offset pagination drifts and skips or repeats rows when the underlying set changes mid-traversal, so large collections need a stable cursor.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent paginates by offset over a changing table, so inserts shift the window and rows are silently duplicated or missed between pages.
problem_solution.solution: A cursor pagination capability that encodes the sort keys into an opaque cursor and returns a next cursor for stable forward traversal.
known_pitfalls: cursor that leaks or trusts client-mutable state
success_signals: no row skipped or repeated across a full traversal
cursor rejected if tampered or malformed

blackbox.does: Returns the ordered version history for a record, optionally between two points, so callers can review or diff how the record changed over time.

problem_solution.problem: Reviewers and support need to see how a record changed and who changed it, in order, and often a diff between two versions rather than raw rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns version rows in arbitrary order without actors or diffs, so the sequence of changes cannot be followed.
problem_solution.solution: A history-read capability that returns versions in order, resolves actors, and can produce a field-level diff between two selected versions.
success_signals: timeline strictly ordered by version
diff reflects only fields that actually changed

blackbox.does: Appends an immutable version entry capturing a record's state, the change actor, and the reason, building an ordered change trail for the record.

problem_solution.problem: Auditable data apps must record every change to a record over time, but mutating rows in place destroys the prior state and any change trail.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the record and logs a free-text note, so prior field values are lost and the trail cannot be reconstructed.
problem_solution.solution: A versioning capability that appends an immutable snapshot with actor and reason on each change, forming an ordered version history.
known_pitfalls: gaps or reuse in the version sequence
storing diffs that cannot reconstruct full state
success_signals: each change yields exactly one new version entry
any historical state is reconstructable from the trail

blackbox.does: Validates a submitted resource draft against its schema and uniqueness constraints, persists a new record, and returns the created resource with its assigned identifier.

problem_solution.problem: Every data application needs to create records from validated input without producing duplicates or partial writes when a request is retried.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-rolls an insert that skips schema validation and uniqueness checks, so retries create duplicate rows and malformed records reach the store.
problem_solution.solution: A create capability that validates the draft, enforces uniqueness, supports an idempotency key, and returns the persisted resource with its identifier.
success_signals: repeated create with same idempotency key yields one row
invalid drafts rejected with field-level errors

blackbox.does: Permanently removes a resource after authorization and dependency checks, resolving cascade or restrict behavior for related records, and reports the outcome.

problem_solution.problem: Hard deletion is irreversible and can orphan or cascade into related records, so it must resolve dependencies and authorization before removing anything.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes a row directly and ignores foreign-key relationships, orphaning children or triggering an unintended cascade that removes unrelated data.
problem_solution.solution: A delete capability that authorizes the request, resolves cascade-or-restrict rules for dependents, deletes atomically, and returns an idempotent outcome.
known_pitfalls: second delete raising instead of a no-op
success_signals: dependents handled per the declared rule
repeat delete returns a stable already-deleted outcome

blackbox.does: Fetches a single resource by its identifier, applies field-level read authorization, and returns the record or a typed not-found result.

problem_solution.problem: Reading a single record must consistently distinguish found, not-found, and forbidden cases and expose only fields the caller is allowed to see.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns a raw row including private columns and treats a missing record as an empty object, masking not-found from callers.
problem_solution.solution: A read capability that resolves by identifier, enforces field-level read policy, and returns a typed present-or-absent result.
known_pitfalls: leaking private fields to unauthorized callers
success_signals: forbidden fields never appear in the response
missing records return an explicit not-found

blackbox.does: Applies a partial patch to an existing resource under an optimistic-concurrency check, validates the merged record, and returns the updated resource.

problem_solution.problem: Concurrent edits to the same record silently overwrite each other unless updates carry a version precondition and validate the merged result.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a blind update with no version check, so a stale client clobbers a newer edit and the lost write goes unnoticed.
problem_solution.solution: An update capability that requires a version or ETag precondition, merges the patch, validates the result, and rejects stale writes with a conflict.
known_pitfalls: lost updates from missing version checks
success_signals: stale writes rejected with a conflict
unspecified fields preserved across the patch

blackbox.does: Reflects a record create, update, or delete into a search index so query results stay consistent with the source records, upserting or removing the affected document.

problem_solution.problem: A search index drifts from the source records whenever a change is not reflected, so stale or deleted records keep showing up in results.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reindexes on create but never on update or delete, so edits do not appear and deleted records remain searchable.
problem_solution.solution: An index-update capability that maps each record delta to an idempotent document upsert or removal, keeping the index consistent with the source.
known_pitfalls: deletes not removed from the index
out-of-order updates leaving a stale document
success_signals: index reflects the latest record state after apply
replaying the same delta leaves the index unchanged

blackbox.does: Reads and writes a scoped set of user or workspace settings against a declared schema with defaults, returning the effective merged settings state.

problem_solution.problem: Settings pages must validate each key against an allowed schema, apply defaults, and scope changes correctly, or they accept unknown keys and leak settings across scopes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent stores an arbitrary settings blob with no schema, so unknown keys accumulate and one user's change bleeds into another scope.
problem_solution.solution: A settings capability that validates keys against a schema, merges over defaults, scopes writes to the owner, and returns the effective state.
known_pitfalls: defaults not applied to missing keys
settings leaking across users or workspaces
success_signals: only schema-known keys accepted
read after write returns the effective merged state

blackbox.does: Marks a resource as deleted with a timestamp and actor instead of removing it, so it disappears from default queries while remaining recoverable.

problem_solution.problem: Records often must be removed from view but stay recoverable for audit or undo, yet default queries keep returning soft-deleted rows unless filtering is consistent.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent adds a deleted flag but forgets to exclude it from list and lookup queries, so soft-deleted records keep appearing everywhere.
problem_solution.solution: A soft-delete capability that sets a deletion marker with timestamp and actor and provides a default scope that hides marked records.
known_pitfalls: default queries still returning deleted rows
unique constraints blocking re-create of a deleted key
second soft-delete overwriting the original timestamp
success_signals: marked records excluded from default reads
repeat soft-delete leaves the first marker intact

blackbox.does: Runs an image-classification model, returning top-k labels with probabilities and the model/version in a receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Classification needs a stable top-k label/probability contract with recorded model and label map.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Returns a single argmax with no probabilities or label-map provenance.
problem_solution.solution: A classify primitive returning top-k labels+probs with a model receipt.
success_signals: top-k with probabilities
label map recorded

blackbox.does: Runs an object-detection model on an image, returning class-labeled boxes with confidences and the model/version in a receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Object detection outputs vary wildly by model; downstream code needs a stable box/label/score contract and provenance.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Emits raw model tensors and forgets to record the model/threshold used.
problem_solution.solution: A detection primitive returning normalized boxes+labels+scores with a model receipt.
success_signals: normalized boxes
model/threshold recorded

blackbox.does: Encodes an image into a fixed-length embedding vector with a named model for similarity search and clustering.

problem_solution.problem: Image search/dedupe needs embeddings from a consistent model with recorded dimensions.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Mixes embeddings from different models/dimensions in one index.
problem_solution.solution: An embed primitive emitting a fixed-dim vector with model+dimension provenance.
success_signals: fixed dimension
model recorded

blackbox.does: Applies non-maximum suppression and confidence thresholding to a detection set, returning de-duplicated bounding boxes.

problem_solution.problem: Detectors emit overlapping duplicate boxes; downstream counting/cropping needs them de-duplicated.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Uses raw detections, double-counting objects.
problem_solution.solution: An NMS primitive with IoU threshold that keeps the highest-confidence box per cluster.
success_signals: no overlapping duplicates above IoU
count stabilizes

blackbox.does: Runs OCR on an image, returning text blocks with bounding boxes and confidences for source-grounded text extraction.

problem_solution.problem: OCR text is only trustworthy with its location; agents often keep the string and drop the box.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Concatenates all OCR text into one blob with no positions or confidences.
problem_solution.solution: An OCR primitive returning positioned text blocks with confidence, enabling source-grounded use.
success_signals: blocks carry boxes+confidence
reading order preserved

blackbox.does: Detects and associates objects across a frame sequence into consistent tracks with stable IDs over time.

problem_solution.problem: Counting/behavior analysis needs stable object identities across frames, not per-frame detections.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Treats each frame independently, so IDs flicker and counts are wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A tracking primitive associating detections into tracks with stable IDs.
success_signals: stable ids across frames
track count plausible

blackbox.does: Appends a batch of source rows to a target table with a dedup guard on a delivery key so a re-delivered batch adds no duplicate rows.

problem_solution.problem: Append-only ingestion into an event or fact table needs a way to stay exactly-once when the upstream delivers a batch more than once.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends every received batch without a delivery-key guard, so retried or replayed batches inflate the table with duplicates.
problem_solution.solution: An append capability that records a delivery key per batch and skips a batch whose key has already been appended.
known_pitfalls: delivery key not persisted across restarts
success_signals: a replayed batch appends zero new rows
each delivery key appears once in the ledger

blackbox.does: Reprocesses a bounded historical time window and rewrites the affected partitions so that a corrected transformation is applied uniformly across that range.

problem_solution.problem: When a transformation is fixed, a bounded historical window must be recomputed and its partitions rewritten without disturbing data outside the window.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reruns the whole pipeline or an unbounded range, rewriting far more than intended and risking loss of correct recent data.
problem_solution.solution: A backfill capability that takes an explicit closed window, recomputes only its partitions, and replaces them transactionally.
known_pitfalls: partial rewrite leaving mixed transformation versions
success_signals: only in-window partitions change
re-running the same window yields identical partitions

blackbox.does: Applies an ordered stream of insert, update, and delete change events to a target table so it converges to the source state, respecting event order per key.

problem_solution.problem: Replicating a source table via a change stream requires applying inserts, updates, and deletes in per-key order so the target converges to the source.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies events as they arrive without per-key ordering or delete handling, so an out-of-order update resurrects a deleted row.
problem_solution.solution: A CDC-apply capability that orders events per key by their commit position and applies inserts, updates, and deletes idempotently.
known_pitfalls: reapplying an event double-counting a change
success_signals: target converges to the source snapshot
replaying the same events changes nothing further

blackbox.does: Recommends sort or clustering key columns for a table from its filter and range-scan patterns and returns a proposed ordering with the columns to cluster by.

problem_solution.problem: Selecting clustering or sort keys so that common filters prune data recurs, and the right choice depends on which columns predicates most often constrain.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent clusters on a rarely filtered column, so predicate pushdown skips almost nothing and scans stay wide.
problem_solution.solution: A planning capability that ranks candidate columns by how often predicates constrain them and proposes a clustering order.
known_pitfalls: clustering on a column filters rarely touch
ignoring correlation that makes a key redundant
success_signals: proposed keys align with the most frequent predicates
plan is advisory with no table rewritten

blackbox.does: Flattens a set of related relations into one wide record per root entity by resolving foreign keys and folding child rows into nested or repeated fields.

problem_solution.problem: Serving and analytics layers often need one wide record per entity, assembled from several normalized relations joined on their keys.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inner-joins the relations and silently drops entities that have no child rows, so the flattened output is missing records.
problem_solution.solution: A denormalize capability that resolves the relation graph from a declared root and folds child rows into nested fields with outer semantics.
known_pitfalls: dropping parents with no children under inner joins
success_signals: every root entity appears once in the output
re-normalizing reproduces the source relations

blackbox.does: Assembles a feature table keyed by an entity and a point-in-time reference, joining source tables so that each feature reflects only data available at that reference.

problem_solution.problem: Model training and serving need a feature table keyed by entity and time where each feature reflects only information available as of that timestamp.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins the latest source values onto historical rows, leaking future information into training features and inflating offline scores.
problem_solution.solution: A feature-build capability that performs point-in-time correct joins from an entity-and-timestamp spine to the source tables.
known_pitfalls: duplicate feature rows per entity-time key
silent nulls where a source has no prior value
success_signals: no feature value postdates its row timestamp
rebuilding the same window reproduces the table

blackbox.does: Groups rows by declared key columns and computes named aggregate measures per group, returning one row per distinct group key.

problem_solution.problem: Rollups and summaries require grouping rows by keys and computing measures, with consistent handling of nulls and empty groups.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes aggregates without deciding how nulls participate, so counts and averages disagree between runs and with the source totals.
problem_solution.solution: A group-aggregate capability that names the group keys and measures and applies a declared null policy per measure.
known_pitfalls: nulls skewing averages when not excluded
group keys with mixed types splitting a group
success_signals: summed measures reconcile with the ungrouped totals
one output row per distinct group key

blackbox.does: Merges a batch of incoming rows into a target table by business key, inserting new keys and updating changed ones, and returns per-outcome counts.

problem_solution.problem: Incremental pipelines must fold each new batch into an existing table by key without creating duplicate rows or overwriting unchanged records.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes-then-inserts the whole key space or appends blindly, producing duplicate keys and losing the ability to re-run a batch safely.
problem_solution.solution: A merge capability keyed on a business identifier that classifies each incoming row as insert or update and applies the change once per key.
known_pitfalls: duplicate keys when the merge key is not unique
non-idempotent re-runs on the same batch
updates clobbering later data on out-of-order batches
success_signals: re-applying a batch yields no additional changes
each business key resolves to exactly one row

blackbox.does: Emits a run lifecycle event describing the job, its input datasets, and its output datasets to a lineage backend so downstream tools can assemble a dataset dependency graph.

problem_solution.problem: Data platforms need every job to declare its input and output datasets so a dependency and provenance graph can be assembled across pipelines.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent logs a freeform message instead of a structured lineage event, so no tool can reconstruct which datasets a run consumed or produced.
problem_solution.solution: A lineage-emit capability that reports start and complete events naming the run and its input and output datasets in a standard event shape.
known_pitfalls: missing a complete event on job failure
unstable dataset names breaking graph edges
success_signals: emitted events validate against the lineage schema
each run has matched start and complete events

blackbox.does: Pivots a long table into wide form by spreading a category column across new columns and placing the associated values under each, aggregating collisions per a declared rule.

problem_solution.problem: Reporting steps need a long table spread into wide form where each distinct category value becomes its own column keyed by the identifier.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent pivots without declaring a collision rule, so duplicate identifier-category pairs raise or silently keep an arbitrary value.
problem_solution.solution: A pivot capability that names the category and value columns and a declared aggregation for collisions, emitting one row per identifier.
known_pitfalls: silent value loss on duplicate identifier-category pairs
exploding column count from a high-cardinality category
success_signals: unpivoting the wide output reproduces the source rows
one output row per distinct identifier

blackbox.does: Splits a flat table with repeating groups into a set of related relations linked by generated surrogate keys so that each fact is stored once.

problem_solution.problem: Flat exports carry repeating groups and redundant attributes that must be split into normalized relations before they can be stored and queried without update anomalies.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent extracts child tables but forgets to mint or wire foreign keys, so the pieces cannot be joined back into the original records.
problem_solution.solution: A normalize capability that factors repeating groups into child relations and links them to the parent with generated keys.
known_pitfalls: orphan child rows from missing foreign keys
collisions when reusing natural keys as surrogates
success_signals: joining the relations back reproduces the flat input
no repeating groups remain in any relation

blackbox.does: Recommends a partition scheme for a table from its column statistics and query patterns and returns a proposed plan with the columns and granularity to partition by.

problem_solution.problem: Choosing partition columns and granularity for a large table recurs, and a poor choice yields tiny fragmented files or a few oversized partitions.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent partitions on a high-cardinality column, producing a partition per key and a small-file explosion that degrades reads.
problem_solution.solution: A planning capability that reads column cardinality and access patterns and proposes a partition scheme within a target file-size band.
known_pitfalls: skewed partitions from an uneven key
success_signals: proposed partitions fall within the target size band
plan is a recommendation with no table mutated

blackbox.does: Merges incoming dimension rows into a type-2 history by closing the prior version of a changed key and opening a new current version with validity intervals.

problem_solution.problem: Dimension tables must preserve history, so a changed attribute should close the current row and open a new version rather than overwrite in place.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent updates the dimension row in place, destroying prior history and leaving fact rows pointing at a version that no longer exists.
problem_solution.solution: A type-2 merge capability that detects attribute changes by key, closes the prior current row, and opens a new version with validity bounds.
known_pitfalls: overlapping validity intervals for one key
multiple rows flagged current for one key
success_signals: exactly one current row per natural key
re-running the same batch opens no new versions

blackbox.does: Joins two tables on declared key columns under a chosen join type and reports match counts and the count of unmatched rows on each side.

problem_solution.problem: Combining two datasets on a shared key recurs everywhere, and the outcome depends on join type and on how unmatched and duplicate keys are handled.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins on a non-unique key without checking cardinality, so the result fans out to more rows than either input and totals silently inflate.
problem_solution.solution: A join capability that takes explicit keys and join type and surfaces match and unmatched-row counts for each side.
known_pitfalls: unexpected row fan-out from non-unique keys
type mismatch making keys never match
null keys matching or dropping unexpectedly
success_signals: output cardinality matches the declared join type
unmatched-row counts are reported, not hidden

blackbox.does: Loads a batch of source rows into a target table under a declared write mode (append or full replace) and returns the resulting row count and write receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Loading a batch of rows into a target table must respect a declared write mode and stay recoverable when the same batch is delivered again after a failure.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent issues an ad-hoc insert with no write-mode contract, so a retried run either double-loads rows or silently truncates the table.
problem_solution.solution: A load capability that takes an explicit append-or-replace mode, validates the source shape against the target schema, and reports the rows written.
known_pitfalls: replace mode truncating on an empty source
source columns silently dropped on shape mismatch
success_signals: re-running the same batch id leaves one copy of the rows
source/target column mismatch is rejected before any write

blackbox.does: Reshapes a wide table into long form by unpivoting a set of value columns into paired variable-name and value columns while preserving the identifier columns.

problem_solution.problem: Analytics and modeling steps repeatedly need a wide table melted into long form so that many metric columns become rows keyed by a variable name.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-writes a melt that forgets to carry the identifier columns or mislabels the variable column, corrupting downstream joins.
problem_solution.solution: A reshape capability that takes explicit identifier and value columns and emits one long row per identifier-and-variable pair.
known_pitfalls: dropping identifier columns during the melt
mixing incompatible value dtypes into one column
success_signals: pivoting the long output back reproduces the source table
row count equals identifiers times value columns

blackbox.does: Computes per-row window measures such as running totals, ranks, and lag or lead within partitions ordered by declared columns, without collapsing rows.

problem_solution.problem: Running totals, ranks, and lag/lead values recur across analytics and must be computed within ordered partitions while keeping every input row.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sorts globally and forgets to partition, so running totals bleed across entities and ranks are computed over the wrong scope.
problem_solution.solution: A window capability that takes partition and ordering columns and a named window measure, emitting one value per input row.
known_pitfalls: ties producing unstable ranks without a tiebreak
success_signals: window values reset at each partition boundary
input and output row counts are equal

blackbox.does: Captures a consistent point-in-time backup of a declared data source to durable storage, recording a checksum and retention window so the artifact can later be verified and expired.

problem_solution.problem: Backups run without consistency guarantees or checksums, so nobody knows whether a captured artifact is restorable until a disaster tests it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies live files while writes are in flight, stores the dump unencrypted, and never records a checksum or retention window.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that captures a consistent snapshot to durable storage with a recorded checksum and retention window.
success_signals: backup is internally consistent
checksum is recorded
artifact is encrypted at rest

blackbox.does: Shifts live traffic to a release candidate in staged increments guarded by health and error thresholds, halting or reverting the progression when a guard breaches.

problem_solution.problem: New releases receive all traffic at once, so a regression reaches every user before any signal shows it is bad.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flips one hundred percent of traffic to the new version immediately, with no metric guard and no automatic revert path.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that advances traffic in staged increments gated by health and error-rate thresholds, halting and reverting on a breach.
known_pitfalls: guards with no baseline to compare against
success_signals: traffic advances only past passing guards
a breach halts or reverts progression
final state is either promoted or reverted

blackbox.does: Deploys a packaged serverless function against a declared trigger, memory, timeout, and concurrency policy, and records the resulting revision so a prior version can be reselected.

problem_solution.problem: Serverless deploys mutate the live function with implicit defaults for memory, timeout, and concurrency, and leave no clean path back to the prior revision.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deploys with default settings, overwrites the live version in place, and cannot roll back because no revision was retained.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that deploys a packaged function under an explicit runtime policy and records the immutable revision for later reselection.
known_pitfalls: mutating live traffic without a canary
success_signals: revision reference is recorded
runtime limits are explicit
prior revision remains reselectable

blackbox.does: Renders a multi-service local orchestration definition from a declared topology, wiring dependencies, health conditions, and named volumes without exposing secrets inline.

problem_solution.problem: Local and CI compose files drift from production topology and hardcode credentials, so services start in the wrong order and fail intermittently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a compose file with no depends_on health conditions and inlines a database password as an environment literal.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders a compose definition from a declared service graph with explicit dependency health gating and externalized secret references.
success_signals: services start in dependency order
no secret literals present
definition validates against the compose schema

blackbox.does: Resolves runtime configuration from an environment mapping against a declared schema, applying defaults and typed coercion and failing fast with a full list of missing or invalid settings.

problem_solution.problem: Applications read configuration from the environment ad hoc, so a missing or misspelled variable surfaces as a runtime crash deep in a request instead of at startup.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads environment variables inline with untyped string access and no defaults, so a missing value becomes a None dereference much later.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that resolves the full config against a schema at startup, coercing types and reporting every missing or invalid setting at once.
known_pitfalls: failing on the first error instead of all of them
reading env deep in request paths
success_signals: invalid config fails fast at startup
every missing setting is listed at once
resolved values are typed

blackbox.does: Produces a reproducible container image build definition from application source and a build policy, pinning a base image and declaring a minimal runtime layer.

problem_solution.problem: Teams hand-write container build files that pull mutable latest tags, bundle build tools into runtime layers, and drift between environments.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies a bloated Dockerfile with an unpinned base image, runs the app as root, and installs a full toolchain into the final layer.
problem_solution.solution: A build-spec capability that emits a pinned, layered, non-root build definition from declared source and policy inputs.
known_pitfalls: no dockerignore so context is huge
success_signals: image rebuilds byte-stable from the same inputs
runtime layer excludes build tools
non-root user is set

blackbox.does: Applies an ordered, versioned schema migration inside a transaction where the engine allows it, recording which migrations ran and pairing each forward change with a declared reverse step.

problem_solution.problem: Schema changes are applied by hand out of order with no reverse step, so environments diverge and a bad change cannot be backed out.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs a raw destructive ALTER directly against production with no version record and no down migration.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies ordered versioned migrations transactionally and records the applied set with a paired reverse step for each.
known_pitfalls: long lock on a large table
success_signals: applied set is recorded in version order
each change has a reverse step
environments converge to the same version

blackbox.does: Authors a CI workflow definition from a declared pipeline intent, pinning action versions, scoping least-privilege permissions, and wiring job dependencies and caches.

problem_solution.problem: CI workflows float action versions by tag, grant a broad default token, and duplicate steps, making pipelines both insecure and hard to change.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent references third-party actions by a mutable tag, keeps write-all token permissions, and copies build steps across jobs.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that authors a workflow with pinned action references, least-privilege permissions, and shared job dependencies.
success_signals: actions pinned to immutable references
permissions are least privilege
workflow validates against the schema

blackbox.does: Renders a per-environment Helm values document from declared chart inputs, layering overrides in a defined precedence order and validating them against the chart values schema.

problem_solution.problem: Helm value overrides accumulate ad hoc across environments with no schema, so a typo silently disables a setting and only surfaces after a release.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent edits a shared values file for one environment, breaking the others, and misspells a key that Helm ignores without error.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders environment-specific values with a defined override precedence and validates them against the chart values schema.
known_pitfalls: sharing one values file across environments
success_signals: values validate against the chart schema
override precedence is deterministic
environments stay isolated

blackbox.does: Renders a Kubernetes Deployment manifest from a workload specification, declaring resource requests and limits, probes, and a rollout strategy with explicit replica counts.

problem_solution.problem: Deployment manifests ship without resource limits or probes, so pods overcommit nodes and traffic routes to instances that are not ready.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a Deployment with no requests, no limits, and no readiness probe, then sets replicas to one with a recreate strategy.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders a Deployment with declared requests and limits, liveness and readiness probes, and a rolling update strategy.
success_signals: manifest passes API schema validation
requests and limits are present
readiness probe gates traffic

blackbox.does: Renders a Kubernetes Job or CronJob manifest for a batch task, declaring a backoff limit, active deadline, and restart policy so the task runs to completion or fails cleanly.

problem_solution.problem: Batch jobs are deployed without deadlines or backoff limits, so a failing task retries forever and never surfaces a terminal failure.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent authors a Job with no backoffLimit and an always restart policy, so a crashing container loops indefinitely.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders a Job manifest with a bounded backoff, an active deadline, and a terminal-failure restart policy.
known_pitfalls: infinite retries with no backoff limit
wrong restart policy for a batch task
success_signals: job reaches a terminal state
failures surface after the backoff limit
manifest validates against the API schema

blackbox.does: Restores a backup artifact into an isolated environment and verifies integrity and row or object counts against expectations, reporting a pass or fail without touching production.

problem_solution.problem: Backups are assumed restorable but never exercised, so the first real restore during an incident is also the first test of the procedure.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent verifies only that the backup file exists on disk, never restoring it, and points the restore at the production target by mistake.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that restores into an isolated environment and checks integrity and counts against expectations.
known_pitfalls: checking file existence instead of contents
no isolation between test and live data
success_signals: restore completes in isolation
counts match expectations
production is untouched

blackbox.does: Reverts a live deployment to a previously recorded known-good revision, verifying that the target revision exists and reporting the health of the reverted state.

problem_solution.problem: When a release fails there is no rehearsed path back, so operators improvise under pressure and sometimes roll forward into a worse state.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent redeploys the last commit from source instead of the previously running artifact, reintroducing an unrelated in-flight change.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that reselects a recorded prior revision as the live target and reports post-revert health.
known_pitfalls: database migration not reversible with the code
success_signals: live target matches the chosen prior revision
revert is idempotent
post-revert health is reported

blackbox.does: Rotates a managed secret by issuing a new version, updating consumers to the new value, and retiring the old version only after consumers confirm they have adopted it.

problem_solution.problem: Long-lived credentials are never rotated, and manual rotations break consumers because the old value is revoked before every service has the new one.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent generates a new secret and immediately deletes the old one, taking down every consumer still holding the previous value.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that stages a new secret version, propagates it to consumers, and retires the old version only after adoption is confirmed.
known_pitfalls: revoking the old version before adoption
success_signals: consumers switch with no outage
old version retired only after adoption
no secret value appears in logs

blackbox.does: Wraps a set of related infrastructure resources into a reusable module with typed input variables, documented outputs, and pinned provider version constraints.

problem_solution.problem: Copy-pasted resource blocks proliferate across stacks with inconsistent variables and no version pins, making changes error-prone to propagate.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent duplicates raw resource blocks per environment, hardcodes region and sizing, and omits provider version constraints.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that packages resources into a reusable module with a typed variable contract, explicit outputs, and provider constraints.
success_signals: module is consumed by multiple stacks unchanged
variables are typed and validated
outputs are documented

blackbox.does: Computes a declarative infrastructure change plan by comparing desired configuration against recorded state and reports the additions, changes, and destructions without applying any of them.

problem_solution.problem: Infrastructure changes are applied without a reviewed diff, so destructive replacements surprise operators and drift accumulates silently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs apply directly, or reads the plan output as prose instead of the machine-readable plan, missing a resource marked for replacement.
problem_solution.solution: A read-only planning capability that emits a structured, reviewable change set and surfaces destroy-and-recreate actions explicitly.
known_pitfalls: reading prose output instead of structured plan
success_signals: plan lists every add, change, and destroy
no resources are mutated during planning
destructive actions are highlighted

blackbox.does: Splits a document into clause and section spans under a declared heading and boundary policy, returning each segment with the character offsets that delimit it.

problem_solution.problem: Field extraction and review work at the clause or section level, so a document must be cut into labeled spans with exact offsets.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent splits on blank lines or fixed lengths, cutting through clauses and producing segments that do not align to real boundaries.
problem_solution.solution: A segmentation capability that applies a declared heading and boundary policy and returns segments with the offsets that bound them.
known_pitfalls: merging two clauses that share a heading style
offsets that drift from the source text
dropping preamble text that precedes the first heading
success_signals: each segment's offsets slice back to its text
clause boundaries align to the declared policy

blackbox.does: Assembles extracted fields, their verbatim source spans, normalization results, and verification verdicts into one evidence bundle a reviewer or auditor can inspect.

problem_solution.problem: Extraction outputs are scattered across values, spans, normalizations, and verdicts, leaving no single artifact an auditor can trust end to end.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hands back only final values, so nobody can see the span, normalization, or verification behind each field.
problem_solution.solution: An evidence-bundling capability that gathers each field with its span, normalization, and verification verdict into one inspectable artifact.
known_pitfalls: bundling a value without its verification verdict
spans that no longer match after normalization
success_signals: every field in the bundle carries span and verdict
failed fields are present and marked, not silently dropped

blackbox.does: Locates a requested field in a document and returns its value bound to the verbatim source span it was read from, or an explicit not-found when the field is absent.

problem_solution.problem: An extracted field value is only trustworthy if it points at the exact span of the document it was read from, and absence must be reported rather than invented.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns a plausible value with no span, so a hallucinated field is indistinguishable from a grounded one.
problem_solution.solution: A locate-and-extract capability that binds every returned value to a verbatim source span and reports not-found instead of guessing.
known_pitfalls: returning a value whose span does not contain it
guessing a value when the field is absent
spans that point at the wrong page or offset
success_signals: every returned value resolves to a verbatim span
absent fields are reported as not-found

blackbox.does: Reads a source document and produces an ordered set of layout blocks with their text and page positions, preserving the coordinates needed to anchor later extractions.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream extraction needs an ordered, position-aware view of a document, but raw files hand back either flat text or nothing anchorable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flattens the document to a text blob, discarding block order and coordinates so no later value can be tied to a location.
problem_solution.solution: An ingest capability that returns ordered layout blocks carrying their text and page positions for later anchoring.
known_pitfalls: losing reading order in multi-column pages
dropping coordinates needed for later spans
silently skipping pages that fail to parse
success_signals: blocks preserve reading order and page positions
every block can be located back on its page
