blackbox.does: Confirms that a claimed source span exists in the document and that the extracted value is actually supported by the text at that span, returning a pass or fail verdict.

problem_solution.problem: An extraction pipeline can only be trusted if every value's claimed span is checked to exist and to actually support the value.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts the extractor's own span without rechecking it, letting fabricated or drifted spans pass as grounded.
problem_solution.solution: A span-verification gate that re-reads the document at the claimed span and confirms the text there supports the extracted value.
known_pitfalls: accepting a span whose text does not contain the value
off-by-one offsets that resolve to neighboring text
passing a span that points outside the document
success_signals: values whose span text does not support them fail the gate
every passing value re-reads to its claimed span

blackbox.does: Recovers the rows and columns of a table region into structured line items, binding each extracted cell value to the verbatim source span it came from.

problem_solution.problem: Line-item tables carry the values that matter most, yet their cells must be recovered into rows and columns without losing the link back to the source.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads a table as free text and reflows cells into the wrong rows, then reports totals that never existed on the page.
problem_solution.solution: A table-extraction capability that reconstructs rows and columns and binds each cell value to its verbatim source span.
known_pitfalls: merging wrapped rows into one line item
reporting a computed total as if it were extracted
success_signals: each cell value resolves to a verbatim span
row and column counts match the source table

blackbox.does: Normalizes an extracted field value such as a date, amount, or identifier into a canonical typed form while preserving the source span of the original raw value.

problem_solution.problem: Extracted values arrive in the document's own formatting, so they must be normalized to typed canonical forms without severing the tie to the original span.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reformats a date or amount and discards the raw span, so the normalized value can no longer be traced back to the page.
problem_solution.solution: A value-normalization capability that canonicalizes typed values while carrying the original raw text and its source span alongside.
known_pitfalls: ambiguous date orders parsed to the wrong day
currency symbols dropped during amount parsing
discarding the source span during normalization
success_signals: the source span survives normalization
the normalized value reparses to the same canonical form

blackbox.does: Checks that every value in a column belongs to a declared allowed set and returns a pass or fail result with a sample of the disallowed values found.

problem_solution.problem: Categorical columns must stay within a known set of codes, and an unexpected value should fail a check rather than flow into logic that only handles known codes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hardcodes the known codes in downstream branches and treats an unseen code as a default, silently misrouting the row.
problem_solution.solution: An accepted-values check that compares the column against a declared set and reports any value outside it.
known_pitfalls: case or whitespace variants flagged as disallowed
nulls neither allowed nor explicitly rejected
allowed set drifting out of sync with the source
success_signals: values outside the set are reported
a conforming column passes with no sample

blackbox.does: Removes duplicate rows sharing a declared key, keeping one survivor per key chosen by a tiebreak rule and reporting how many rows were dropped per key.

problem_solution.problem: Datasets accumulate duplicate rows for a key, and collapsing them requires a deterministic rule for which duplicate survives.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent drops duplicates with no ordering, so which row survives varies between runs and downstream values flip nondeterministically.
problem_solution.solution: A dedupe capability that groups by the key and keeps the survivor selected by a declared tiebreak, reporting the dropped count.
success_signals: one row remains per key
re-running the dedupe removes no further rows

blackbox.does: Summarizes a column distribution with count, distinct count, min and max, and quantiles for numeric data or top categories for categorical data.

problem_solution.problem: Column-level distribution summaries recur as the baseline for quality checks and monitoring, and they must handle numeric and categorical columns distinctly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes numeric statistics on a categorical column or reports a mean of encoded codes, producing meaningless summaries.
problem_solution.solution: A profiling capability that branches on column kind and emits quantiles for numeric columns and top-category frequencies for categorical ones.
known_pitfalls: quantiles on a column with heavy ties
high-cardinality categories overwhelming the top list
success_signals: reported counts reconcile with the row count
recomputing yields the same summary

blackbox.does: Checks that the newest load or event timestamp in a dataset is within a declared maximum age relative to a reference time and returns the observed lag.

problem_solution.problem: A pipeline can stop delivering while its table still returns stale rows, so freshness must be checked against the newest timestamp and a maximum allowed age.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks that the table has rows but never checks recency, so a silently stalled feed passes while serving old data.
problem_solution.solution: A freshness check that computes the lag between the newest timestamp and a reference time and fails when it exceeds the allowed age.
known_pitfalls: timezone mismatch inflating or hiding lag
reference time hardcoded instead of current
success_signals: a stalled feed fails on lag
a recently loaded table passes with reported lag

blackbox.does: Checks that a required column contains no null or null-equivalent values and returns a pass or fail result with the count and a sample of offending rows.

problem_solution.problem: Required columns must never be null, and a check is needed to fail a load rather than let missing mandatory values reach downstream consumers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent tests only literal nulls and misses empty strings or placeholder sentinels, so effectively missing values pass the check.
problem_solution.solution: A not-null check that fails when any row holds a null-equivalent value in the required column and reports the offending count.
known_pitfalls: sentinel placeholders not treated as null
success_signals: missing required values fail the check
a fully populated column passes

blackbox.does: Profiles a dataset for missingness, reporting the null count and null fraction per column and the count of fully-null rows across the dataset.

problem_solution.problem: Understanding missingness per column recurs before any modeling or reporting, and it must count nulls consistently including empty-string and placeholder cases.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent counts only literal nulls and misses empty strings and sentinel placeholders, so columns look complete when they are not.
problem_solution.solution: A profiling capability that reports null counts and fractions per column under a declared set of null-equivalent values.
known_pitfalls: empty strings not counted as null
success_signals: null counts reconcile with total row count
recomputing yields identical fractions

blackbox.does: Flags values in a numeric column that fall outside a declared bound derived from a robust statistic, returning per-row flags and the thresholds used.

problem_solution.problem: Numeric columns carry data-entry and pipeline errors that surface as extreme values, and flagging them recurs before aggregation or modeling.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent thresholds on the mean and standard deviation, which the very outliers inflate, so extreme values hide themselves.
problem_solution.solution: A flagging capability that bounds values with a robust statistic such as the interquartile range and reports the thresholds it used.
known_pitfalls: mean-based bounds masked by the outliers
empty or constant columns dividing by zero
success_signals: reported thresholds reproduce the flags
flag decisions are stable on the same input

blackbox.does: Aggregates the outcomes of a batch of data-quality checks into a single receipt recording each check, its result, and an overall pass or fail verdict.

problem_solution.problem: A run executes many quality checks, and their outcomes must be consolidated into one durable receipt that gates promotion and records what was verified.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent logs each check result to stdout with no consolidated artifact, so there is no single record to gate on or audit later.
problem_solution.solution: A receipt-emit capability that collects per-check outcomes into one structured artifact with an overall verdict and the dataset reference checked.
known_pitfalls: overall verdict passing while a check failed
receipt missing the dataset or run reference
results overwritten instead of appended per run
success_signals: the receipt lists every check with its result
any failed check makes the overall verdict fail

blackbox.does: Checks that numeric or temporal column values fall within declared inclusive or exclusive bounds and returns a pass or fail result with a sample of out-of-range values.

problem_solution.problem: Numeric and date columns have known valid ranges, and values outside them signal errors that should fail a check before they distort aggregates.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies a range test without pinning boundary inclusivity, so values exactly on the bound pass or fail inconsistently.
problem_solution.solution: A range check that compares each value to declared bounds with explicit inclusivity and reports the out-of-range values.
known_pitfalls: mixed units making the bounds meaningless
success_signals: out-of-range values are reported when present
an in-range column passes

blackbox.does: Checks that every foreign-key value in a child table resolves to an existing key in a parent table and returns the count and a sample of orphan values.

problem_solution.problem: Foreign keys can point at parent rows that do not exist, and these orphans break joins and rollups unless a check catches them at load time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inner-joins child to parent and never notices the orphans that the join silently drops, so counts quietly shrink.
problem_solution.solution: An integrity check that verifies each child foreign key exists in the parent key set and reports orphan values.
known_pitfalls: nulls in the foreign key treated as orphans or ignored inconsistently
type mismatch making every key look orphaned
success_signals: orphan foreign keys are reported when present
a fully referential child passes

blackbox.does: Reconciles the row count between a source and a target dataset within a declared tolerance and returns the difference and a pass or fail result.

problem_solution.problem: A transformation can silently drop or duplicate rows, so source and target counts must be reconciled within tolerance to catch loss or inflation.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assumes counts match after a load and never compares them, so a partial load that lost rows goes unnoticed.
problem_solution.solution: A reconcile check that compares source and target counts under a declared exact-or-tolerance rule and reports the difference.
known_pitfalls: counting after a filter that legitimately drops rows
tolerance so wide it hides real loss
counts taken at different points in time
success_signals: a lossy load fails reconciliation
matching counts pass within tolerance

blackbox.does: Compares an observed dataset schema against an expected baseline and reports added, removed, renamed, and retyped columns classified as breaking or compatible.

problem_solution.problem: Upstream schema changes silently break pipelines, so each load must be compared to an expected baseline and classified before it flows downstream.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent only checks that expected columns exist and misses type changes and added columns, so a breaking retype slips through.
problem_solution.solution: A drift-detect capability that diffs observed against expected schema and labels each change as breaking or compatible.
known_pitfalls: type widening flagged as breaking or vice versa
renamed columns reported as drop plus add
success_signals: breaking changes are surfaced before the load proceeds
a matching schema reports no drift

blackbox.does: Derives a stable fingerprint of a dataset schema from its ordered column names and types so that two datasets can be compared for structural equivalence.

problem_solution.problem: Detecting whether a dataset schema has changed requires a stable, comparable fingerprint of its columns and types rather than an ad-hoc string.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares column lists as unordered strings that shift with formatting, so cosmetic changes read as real drift and vice versa.
problem_solution.solution: A fingerprint capability that canonicalizes column names and types into a deterministic digest for equivalence comparison.
known_pitfalls: column order treated as insignificant when it matters
success_signals: identical schemas produce identical fingerprints
recomputing on the same schema is stable

blackbox.does: Normalizes a text column by applying declared steps such as Unicode normalization, whitespace trimming, and case folding to produce comparable canonical values.

problem_solution.problem: Text values that should be equal differ by whitespace, case, and Unicode form, so comparisons and joins fail until the text is canonicalized.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent lowercases only and skips Unicode normalization, so visually identical strings with different code points still compare unequal.
problem_solution.solution: A normalize capability that applies a declared ordered pipeline of Unicode, whitespace, and case steps to yield canonical text.
known_pitfalls: skipping Unicode normalization before case folding
success_signals: applying the normalizer twice changes nothing further
equivalent inputs map to one canonical value

blackbox.does: Coerces string-typed columns to declared target types such as integer, decimal, boolean, and timestamp, routing values that cannot be parsed to a reject channel.

problem_solution.problem: Ingested data arrives as strings that must become typed values, and unparseable entries need an explicit path rather than a silent null or a crash.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent coerces with a bare cast that turns bad values into nulls, erasing the signal that a column has malformed data.
problem_solution.solution: A coercion capability that parses each column to its declared type under explicit formats and routes unparseable values to a reject channel.
known_pitfalls: bad values silently coerced to null
success_signals: unparseable values land in the reject channel
coerced columns match their declared types

blackbox.does: Checks that a column or column combination is unique across the dataset and returns a pass or fail result with a sample of duplicated key values.

problem_solution.problem: A primary or business key must be unique, and a violation should fail a check with evidence rather than surface later as a fan-out during a join.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assumes a key is unique and joins on it, so a hidden duplicate silently multiplies rows downstream instead of being caught.
problem_solution.solution: A uniqueness check that groups by the key, fails when any group exceeds one row, and returns a sample of the offending keys.
known_pitfalls: null keys excluded or included inconsistently
case or whitespace variants treated as distinct
success_signals: duplicated keys are reported when present
a unique key passes with no sample

blackbox.does: Enriches company records with firmographics (industry, size, identifiers) from a source, recording which field came from which source and when.

problem_solution.problem: Company enrichment must attribute each added field to a source and time, or it becomes untraceable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Overwrites fields without recording the source or freshness, mixing stale and fresh data.
problem_solution.solution: An enrich primitive that records per-field source, timestamp, and conflict flags.
success_signals: each field has source+timestamp
conflicts flagged

blackbox.does: Assigns a per-field confidence to an enriched record set from source authority, agreement across sources, and freshness, flagging fields needing review.

problem_solution.problem: Enriched fields have varying trustworthiness; downstream needs a confidence and a review flag, not a flat merge.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Treats all enriched values as equally true regardless of source or agreement.
problem_solution.solution: A confidence primitive scoring each field by authority, agreement, and freshness with a review flag.
common_outputs: records with per-field confidence + review flags
success_signals: confidence in [0,1] per field
low-confidence flagged for review

blackbox.does: Adds latitude/longitude and match confidence to records with addresses, honoring provider usage policy and recording per-field provenance.

problem_solution.problem: Adding coordinates to address records needs rate-limit-safe geocoding with confidence and provenance.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Hammers a public geocoder past its usage policy and keeps low-confidence matches silently.
problem_solution.solution: A geocode-enrich primitive with usage-policy gate, confidence, and per-field provenance.
success_signals: coordinates added with confidence
provenance recorded

blackbox.does: Combines the evidence signals behind a value, such as source authority, agreement, and freshness, into a bounded confidence score with the contributing factors reported.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream consumers need one comparable confidence number per value, derived from its evidence, not an opaque hunch.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent attaches a round-number confidence with no basis, so the score cannot be compared or explained across values.
problem_solution.solution: A confidence-scoring capability that folds declared evidence signals into a bounded score and reports which factors moved it.
known_pitfalls: scores that exceed the intended bounds
hidden weighting that cannot be inspected
treating missing evidence as strong evidence
success_signals: scores stay within the declared bounds
the reported factors explain each score

blackbox.does: Compares the values several sources report for the same entity attribute and produces a report of where they agree, where they conflict, and how the conflicts break down.

problem_solution.problem: When several sources describe the same attribute, disagreements must be surfaced explicitly rather than hidden by whichever source was read last.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites values as it reads each source, ending with one value and no record that the sources ever disagreed.
problem_solution.solution: A conflict-reporting capability that aligns per-source values for each attribute and reports agreement and conflict structure without silently picking a winner.
known_pitfalls: counting formatting differences as real conflicts
hiding conflicts by resolving them prematurely
ignoring source recency when describing a conflict
success_signals: genuine value disagreements appear as explicit conflicts
normalization-only differences are not reported as conflicts

blackbox.does: Checks a claim about an entity against supplied source passages and returns a supported, refuted, or not-enough-evidence verdict tied to the specific passages that justify it.

problem_solution.problem: A claim about an entity is only trustworthy if it is checked against sources, and the verdict must point at the exact evidence that supports or refutes it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent asserts a claim is true from prior belief without citing a passage, producing a confident but ungrounded verdict.
problem_solution.solution: A source-backed verification capability that compares the claim to supplied passages and returns a verdict bound to the justifying evidence.
known_pitfalls: labeling supported without an evidence passage
confusing absence of evidence with refutation
verdicts that drift when the passage set is unchanged
success_signals: every supported or refuted verdict cites a specific passage
insufficient evidence is labeled as such rather than guessed

blackbox.does: Fetches additional attributes for an entity from a declared reference source and attaches each enriched value with the source it came from and the time it was retrieved.

problem_solution.problem: Records often lack attributes that live in a reference source, and pulling them in without recording where and when they came from destroys auditability.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent scrapes a value and overwrites the record in place with no source or timestamp, so the enrichment can never be traced or refreshed.
problem_solution.solution: An enrichment capability that resolves the entity against a declared source and attaches each new value with its source and retrieval time.
known_pitfalls: attaching an attribute from a mismatched entity
enriching without recording the source or retrieval time
silently overwriting a locally verified value
success_signals: every enriched field carries its source and retrieval time
enrichment leaves original values distinguishable from added ones

blackbox.does: Flags entity values whose age exceeds a declared window or whose meaning depends on a moving reference time, marking them as stale or fragile for revalidation.

problem_solution.problem: Some values silently expire and others are only true relative to a moment, so a system must know which values are stale or context-fragile before trusting them.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent treats every stored value as current, reasoning over an address or status that quietly went stale months ago.
problem_solution.solution: A freshness and fragility detector that compares value age to a declared window and flags values whose truth depends on a moving reference time.
known_pitfalls: a single global window applied to fields with different lifespans
treating a relative-time value as if it were absolute
success_signals: values past their window are flagged stale
context-relative values are marked fragile for revalidation

blackbox.does: Confirms an entity attribute against a declared authoritative registry and returns a match, mismatch, or not-found verdict with the registry response captured as evidence.

problem_solution.problem: Some attributes must be confirmed against an official registry rather than a general source, and the registry response has to be captured as durable evidence.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent treats any web result as authoritative and records a bare yes/no without the registry response behind it.
problem_solution.solution: An official-source verification capability that queries a declared authoritative registry and returns a verdict alongside the captured response.
known_pitfalls: treating a non-authoritative mirror as official
caching a registry response past its validity
recording a verdict with no captured evidence
success_signals: each verdict retains the registry response that produced it
not-found is distinguished from mismatch

blackbox.does: Derives one or more deterministic blocking keys from a standardized record so that only records sharing a key are compared, shrinking the comparison space without scanning all pairs.

problem_solution.problem: Comparing every pair of records grows quadratically, so linkage needs a way to only compare records that could plausibly match.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent either compares all pairs and stalls, or picks one brittle key that scatters true matches across different blocks.
problem_solution.solution: A blocking-key generator that emits several complementary deterministic keys per record to keep true matches in a shared block.
known_pitfalls: a single key so coarse it recreates the all-pairs problem
keys so tight that true matches never share a block
keys built on fields that are frequently missing
success_signals: the same record always yields the same key set
known matched pairs share at least one blocking key

blackbox.does: Enumerates the deduplicated set of candidate record pairs implied by shared blocking keys, so downstream comparison only runs on plausibly matching pairs.

problem_solution.problem: Records that share several blocking keys must be turned into a pair list without emitting the same pair many times or comparing a record with itself.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent expands blocks with a nested loop and emits duplicate and self pairs, inflating the comparison workload.
problem_solution.solution: A candidate-pair generator that expands blocks into an ordered, self-excluding, deduplicated pair set.
known_pitfalls: emitting a pair once per shared key instead of once total
success_signals: each unordered pair appears exactly once
no record is paired with itself

blackbox.does: Builds one canonical entity record for a cluster by selecting surviving field values under declared survivorship rules and records the provenance of every chosen value.

problem_solution.problem: Once records are clustered, the group must collapse into one golden record whose every field is chosen by a defensible rule with traceable provenance.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent picks the first or longest value per field with no rule, producing a golden record no one can justify or audit.
problem_solution.solution: A survivorship capability that applies declared per-field selection rules and attaches the source of each surviving value.
known_pitfalls: overwriting a verified value with a fresher but wrong one
losing provenance for the surviving values
silent conflicts when two sources disagree strongly
success_signals: every surviving field carries its source provenance
the same cluster and rules yield the same canonical record

blackbox.does: Assembles a reviewer packet for borderline pairs in the clerical band, presenting the aligned fields, comparison signals, and score so a human can accept or reject the link.

problem_solution.problem: Pairs in the review band cannot be auto-decided, so a reviewer needs a consistent packet with the evidence needed to accept or reject each link.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent dumps raw record blobs at a reviewer with no aligned fields or score context, making review slow and inconsistent.
problem_solution.solution: A review-packet builder that lays out aligned fields, comparison signals, and the score for each borderline pair in a stable review shape.
known_pitfalls: hiding the disagreeing fields that drove the borderline score
packets that omit the source record identifiers
presenting pairs with no way to record a decision
success_signals: every packet shows the aligned fields and the driving signals
each pair has an explicit accept or reject slot

blackbox.does: Compares the aligned fields of a candidate record pair with declared per-field comparators and emits a structured comparison vector of agreement levels for scoring.

problem_solution.problem: A match model needs a consistent per-field agreement signal, not raw strings, and each field type needs its own notion of agreement.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-codes exact-equality per field, collapsing near matches to disagreement and starving the model of signal.
problem_solution.solution: A comparison-vector emitter that runs a declared comparator per field and returns discrete agreement levels in a fixed vector shape.
known_pitfalls: treating a missing field as disagreement rather than unknown
using one comparator for fields of different types
success_signals: identical pairs always produce the same vector
vector length and field order are stable across pairs

blackbox.does: Normalizes a postal address, phone number, or email address into a canonical comparable form using the declared field type and region, and reports which normalization rules fired.

problem_solution.problem: Postal addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses each have their own formatting variation that defeats plain string comparison during linkage.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent strips punctuation blindly, mangling extension digits or address unit designators, and matches on the broken result.
problem_solution.solution: A contact-point normalizer that dispatches by field type to canonicalize addresses, phones, and emails into comparable forms.
known_pitfalls: assuming a national phone region when it is unknown
lowercasing email local parts where case is significant
collapsing distinct address units into one
success_signals: formatting-only variants normalize to the same value
region-specific inputs canonicalize without losing digits

blackbox.does: Resolves accepted pairwise links into consistent entity clusters, applying the declared transitivity policy so that grouped records agree on membership.

problem_solution.problem: Pairwise match decisions can conflict, so links must be resolved into clusters where membership is consistent and a merge decision is deliberate.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent takes the transitive closure of every weak link, chaining unrelated records into one giant over-merged blob.
problem_solution.solution: A clustering capability that groups accepted links under an explicit transitivity or graph-resolution policy and reports cluster sizes.
known_pitfalls: transitive over-merging through a single weak bridge link
success_signals: cluster membership is stable given the same links
no cluster forms solely through a below-threshold bridge

blackbox.does: Selects match and non-match score thresholds from scored pairs and a labeled sample, reporting the resulting agreement and review-band sizes at the chosen cut points.

problem_solution.problem: A raw match score is only useful once cut points separate automatic matches, automatic non-matches, and a clerical review band, and those cuts govern who gets merged.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes a single threshold from intuition, silently auto-merging borderline pairs that should have gone to review.
problem_solution.solution: A threshold-tuning capability that derives upper and lower cut points from labeled pairs and reports the band each cut produces.
known_pitfalls: tuning on a sample that is not representative
collapsing the review band to zero and auto-merging borderlines
leaking labels from the sample into the same evaluation
success_signals: chosen thresholds reproduce on a held-out labeled slice
the review band is explicit and non-empty when labels are ambiguous

blackbox.does: Parses a person or organization name into standardized components, folds diacritics and legal-form suffixes, and emits a comparable normalized form alongside the parsed parts.

problem_solution.problem: Names vary by ordering, casing, diacritics, particles, and legal-form suffixes, so raw string equality misses obvious matches.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares names with a plain lowercase equality and treats every diacritic or suffix variant as a different entity.
problem_solution.solution: A name-normalization capability that parses components, folds diacritics and suffixes, and returns a stable comparable form.
known_pitfalls: over-folding names where diacritics are significant
confusing organization and person parsing rules
success_signals: diacritic and suffix variants of one name normalize identically
parsed components round-trip back to the input tokens

blackbox.does: Turns a comparison vector into a match weight and probability under a Fellegi-Sunter style parameter set, reporting the per-field contributions that produced the score.

problem_solution.problem: Given a comparison vector, linkage needs a principled, explainable match probability rather than an ad-hoc weighted sum.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent invents arbitrary field weights, so scores are unexplainable and drift whenever the weights are nudged.
problem_solution.solution: A probabilistic scorer that applies match and unmatch parameters to each agreement level and returns a weight, probability, and contribution breakdown.
known_pitfalls: reporting a probability with no contribution trace
success_signals: the same vector and parameters always score identically
the reported contributions sum to the total weight

blackbox.does: Cleans a raw entity record into a stable standard shape by trimming whitespace, unifying casing, coercing types, and mapping recognized null tokens to a single missing marker.

problem_solution.problem: Records arriving from many systems carry inconsistent casing, stray whitespace, mixed types, and a zoo of placeholder null tokens that break downstream matching.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes one-off cleanup snippets per feed, so the same field is standardized differently in two places and comparisons silently miss.
problem_solution.solution: A single record-standardization capability that applies a declared, order-stable set of cleaning rules and marks every touched field.
known_pitfalls: coercing numeric-looking codes and dropping leading zeros
treating a legitimate value as a null token
success_signals: re-running the cleaner on its own output changes nothing
the same field cleans identically across every feed

blackbox.does: Decodes Avro-encoded records against their writer schema and emits JSON objects, resolving unions, enums, and logical types to their JSON representations.

problem_solution.problem: Avro records must be rendered as JSON for inspection and downstream tooling, and the schema-driven encoding of unions and logical types has to be resolved correctly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent decodes without the writer schema and mishandles union branches or logical types, producing ambiguous or wrongly typed JSON.
problem_solution.solution: A decode capability that reads records against their writer schema and maps unions, enums, and logical types to explicit JSON forms.
known_pitfalls: union branch ambiguity without the schema
logical types rendered as raw integers
byte fields not encoded for JSON
success_signals: decoded JSON validates against the schema shape
re-encoding under the schema reproduces the values

blackbox.does: Reads a delimited text file with a declared or inferred schema and writes an equivalent columnar Parquet file that preserves the row values and column types.

problem_solution.problem: Delimited text files must become columnar Parquet for efficient analytics, and the conversion has to fix column types rather than leave everything as strings.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes every column as a string or lets type inference guess inconsistently across chunks, corrupting numeric and date columns.
problem_solution.solution: A conversion capability that applies a declared or inferred schema uniformly and writes typed Parquet with the same row set.
success_signals: reading the Parquet reproduces the source row set
column types match the declared schema

blackbox.does: Extracts a rectangular table from a named sheet and cell range of a spreadsheet workbook, applying a header row and returning typed rows with reported cells.

problem_solution.problem: Spreadsheets carry a table inside a sheet surrounded by titles and notes, so extraction must target a specific sheet and range and apply the header explicitly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads the whole sheet from cell one, pulling titles and blank rows into the data and misaligning the header.
problem_solution.solution: An extract capability that takes a sheet name and cell range, applies a declared header row, and returns typed rows.
known_pitfalls: hidden rows or columns included unexpectedly
success_signals: extracted rows match the fixture table
header maps to the declared column names

blackbox.does: Flattens a GeoJSON feature collection into a table with one row per feature, projecting property keys to columns and carrying the geometry in a declared encoding.

problem_solution.problem: GeoJSON feature collections must become a flat feature table where properties are columns and each feature keeps its geometry in a consistent encoding.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps only the properties and drops the geometry, or mixes geometry types into one column without recording the type.
problem_solution.solution: A flatten capability that emits one row per feature with property columns and geometry serialized in a declared encoding alongside its type.
known_pitfalls: mixed geometry types with no type column
success_signals: one table row per input feature
geometry re-parses to the source coordinates

blackbox.does: Flattens a JSON document or array of objects into tabular rows using a declared path mapping, projecting nested fields into named columns.

problem_solution.problem: Nested JSON must be flattened into rows for tabular tools, and the mapping from nested paths to columns has to be explicit and stable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flattens with implicit key concatenation that changes when a field is absent, so columns shift between records.
problem_solution.solution: A flatten capability that maps declared JSON paths to named columns and emits a stable row per input object.
known_pitfalls: column drift when optional fields are missing
arrays silently truncated to the first element
type coercion of numbers to strings
success_signals: every object yields one row with the mapped columns
re-encoding the rows reproduces the mapped fields

blackbox.does: Reads a JSON-Lines file where each line is one record and assembles a table by unioning the observed keys into columns under a declared schema policy.

problem_solution.problem: Line-delimited JSON records must be assembled into a single table even when records carry different subsets of keys across lines.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent takes columns from the first record only, so keys that appear later are dropped and rows misalign.
problem_solution.solution: A load capability that unions keys across records into a stable column set and fills absent keys with a declared null.
known_pitfalls: columns taken from the first record only
one malformed line aborting the whole file
type drift for a key across records
success_signals: every record contributes one row
writing the table back as JSONL reproduces the records

blackbox.does: Splits a newline-delimited JSON file into ordered shard files bounded by a maximum record count or byte size per shard, never splitting a record across shards.

problem_solution.problem: A large NDJSON file must be split into bounded shards for parallel processing, and no shard may contain a partial record.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent splits on a fixed byte offset that lands mid-record, producing shards with a truncated first or last line.
problem_solution.solution: A split capability that packs whole records into ordered shards up to a record-count or byte bound, preserving record boundaries.
known_pitfalls: a record split across two shards
shard order lost by unpadded numbering
trailing newline creating an empty final record
success_signals: concatenating the shards in order reproduces the input
every shard line parses as a complete record

blackbox.does: Reads a Parquet file into an in-memory Arrow table, preserving the column schema and null masks so downstream columnar operations can run without recopying.

problem_solution.problem: Columnar processing needs Parquet data as an in-memory Arrow table with types and null masks intact rather than reflattened into row objects.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads Parquet into row dictionaries and back, losing the columnar layout and the exact type and null information.
problem_solution.solution: A read capability that maps Parquet column types to their Arrow equivalents and preserves null masks in the resulting table.
known_pitfalls: logical types collapsed to physical types
null masks lost through a row-dict detour
nested list and struct columns flattened
success_signals: arrow schema matches the parquet schema
writing the arrow table back reproduces the parquet values

blackbox.does: Exports a Parquet file to a delimited text file with a header row, rendering typed columns to text under declared null, date, and quoting conventions.

problem_solution.problem: Columnar Parquet must be exported to delimited text for tools that only read CSV, and typed values need consistent text rendering and quoting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent renders nulls, floats, and dates inconsistently and skips quoting, so values containing the delimiter corrupt the layout.
problem_solution.solution: An export capability that renders each column to text under declared null, date, and quoting rules and writes a header row.
known_pitfalls: nulls and empty strings made indistinguishable
success_signals: reloading the CSV under the schema reproduces the rows
delimiter-bearing values survive a round trip

blackbox.does: Decodes Protocol Buffers messages against their descriptor and emits JSON following the canonical field-name and value mapping, including default and repeated fields.

problem_solution.problem: Binary Protocol Buffers messages must be turned into JSON for logging and interchange using the canonical mapping so field names and scalar types are consistent.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent maps field numbers instead of the canonical JSON names or omits fields left at their default, so the JSON is unreadable or lossy.
problem_solution.solution: A decode capability that uses the message descriptor to emit canonical JSON with proper field names and value encodings.
known_pitfalls: field numbers exposed instead of names
sixty-four-bit integers losing precision as JSON numbers
unset fields conflated with default values
success_signals: output matches the canonical proto3 JSON mapping
re-encoding the JSON reproduces the message

blackbox.does: Encodes tabular rows into a JSON array of objects, mapping columns to keys and optionally nesting grouped columns into sub-objects per a declared shape.

problem_solution.problem: Tabular rows must be serialized to JSON for APIs and messaging, and column-to-key mapping plus null and type handling has to be consistent.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent emits nulls as the string None or drops null columns entirely, so consumers cannot distinguish absent from empty.
problem_solution.solution: An encode capability that maps columns to keys under a declared shape and represents nulls and types consistently.
known_pitfalls: non-JSON types like dates left unencoded
success_signals: parsing the JSON reproduces the source rows
nulls round-trip as JSON null

blackbox.does: Encodes tabular rows into a newline-delimited JSON file with one JSON object per line, mapping columns to keys under a consistent null and type representation.

problem_solution.problem: Rows must be written as line-delimited JSON for streaming consumers, with exactly one self-contained object per line and stable key mapping.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent pretty-prints records across multiple lines or emits a JSON array, breaking line-by-line consumers.
problem_solution.solution: An encode capability that writes one compact JSON object per line with a declared column-to-key mapping and null representation.
known_pitfalls: an array wrapper breaking streaming reads
success_signals: each line parses to one record
reading the file back reproduces the rows

blackbox.does: Parses an XML document against a declared element-to-field mapping and produces typed records, distinguishing element text, attributes, and repeated child elements.

problem_solution.problem: XML payloads must be mapped into typed records, and the mapping has to treat attributes, element text, and repeated children distinctly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent conflates attributes with child elements or assumes a repeated element occurs once, so records lose fields or collapse lists.
problem_solution.solution: A mapping capability that binds declared element paths and attributes to typed fields and collects repeated elements into lists.
known_pitfalls: attributes lost when only text is read
single vs list ambiguity for repeated elements
success_signals: mapped fields match the fixture expectations
repeated elements always resolve to a list

blackbox.does: Compares served demand against supply across an area and ranks the locations with the largest unmet demand, returning the gaps ordered by a declared coverage measure.

problem_solution.problem: Deciding where to add supply needs the places where demand is served worst, ranked by a consistent coverage measure rather than by intuition.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent ranks by raw demand and ignores existing supply, pointing at busy but already well-served areas as if they were gaps.
problem_solution.solution: A coverage-gap capability that nets demand against supply per location and ranks the largest unmet-demand gaps by a declared measure.
known_pitfalls: ranking by demand alone and ignoring existing supply
mixing incompatible units of demand and supply
success_signals: ranked gaps reflect unmet demand after supply is netted
the same inputs and measure produce the same ranking

blackbox.does: Reprojects geometries from a source coordinate reference system to a target one, recording both systems so downstream operations know the frame the coordinates are in.

problem_solution.problem: Spatial operations are only correct when every layer shares a coordinate reference system, and reprojection that loses track of the frame corrupts later joins and distances.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent mixes geographic and projected coordinates or reprojects without recording the target system, so downstream math runs in the wrong frame.
problem_solution.solution: A reprojection capability that transforms geometry between declared source and target systems and records both frames with the output.
known_pitfalls: swapping latitude and longitude axis order
reprojecting without recording the target frame
assuming a default frame when the source is unlabeled
success_signals: output records the frame its coordinates are in
reprojecting back to the source frame recovers the geometry

blackbox.does: Decides whether an address may be geocoded by checking the declared license, consent, and precision policy, returning an allow or deny decision with the reason and the permitted precision.

problem_solution.problem: Geocoding an address can violate a provider license or a person's consent, so the decision to geocode must be gated by an explicit policy before any lookup runs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent geocodes every address it sees at full precision, ignoring license terms and consent and exposing the pipeline to policy violations.
problem_solution.solution: A policy-gate capability that evaluates license, consent, and precision rules and returns an allow or deny decision with the permitted precision.
known_pitfalls: geocoding at finer precision than policy allows
ignoring a withdrawn or absent consent record
caching a coordinate whose license forbids storage
success_signals: denied addresses never reach the geocoder
allowed results respect the permitted precision

blackbox.does: Computes the area reachable from an origin within a travel-time or distance budget for a declared mode and returns it as a polygon with the budget and mode recorded.

problem_solution.problem: Access questions need the region reachable within a time or distance budget, not just straight-line radius, and that depends on the travel mode and network.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent draws a circle of fixed radius and calls it reachability, ignoring the road or transit network and the travel mode entirely.
problem_solution.solution: An isochrone capability that computes a mode-specific reachability polygon for a declared budget and records the budget and mode.
known_pitfalls: approximating reachability with a straight-line radius
mismatching the mode to the requested budget
returning a polygon without the budget it represents
success_signals: the polygon reflects the declared mode and budget
the output records the budget it was computed for

blackbox.does: Renders geographic layers into a shareable map artifact under a declared style and extent, recording the layers, style, and reference system used to produce it.

problem_solution.problem: Analysis results need a shareable map, but a map produced without recording its layers, style, and frame cannot be reproduced or trusted.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent exports a one-off image with no record of the layers or extent, so the map cannot be regenerated or checked against its inputs.
problem_solution.solution: A map-rendering capability that draws declared layers under a declared style and extent and records what produced the artifact.
known_pitfalls: rendering layers in mismatched reference systems
an extent that clips the features of interest
producing an artifact with no record of its inputs
success_signals: the artifact records the layers, style, and frame used
re-rendering from the same inputs yields the same map

blackbox.does: Assigns each demand point to its nearest facility under a declared distance measure and rolls the assignments up into per-facility catchments with their counts.

problem_solution.problem: Planning questions ask which facility serves each location and how large each facility's catchment is, which requires a consistent nearest-assignment rule.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares raw latitude and longitude differences as if they were planar distance, so nearest assignments are wrong away from the equator.
problem_solution.solution: A nearest-facility capability that assigns demand points under a declared distance measure and aggregates them into per-facility catchments.
known_pitfalls: using planar distance on geographic coordinates
ignoring facility capacity when it matters
success_signals: each demand point maps to its nearest facility under the measure
catchment counts sum to the assigned demand points

blackbox.does: Assigns each point to the boundary polygon that contains it under a shared reference system, reporting points that fall in no boundary or on a shared edge.

problem_solution.problem: Points must be attributed to the administrative or service boundary that contains them, and mismatched reference systems make the containment test silently wrong.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins points and polygons whose coordinate systems differ, so containment is computed on misaligned geometry and every assignment is off.
problem_solution.solution: A point-in-polygon join that operates in a shared reference system and reports points with no boundary or ambiguous edge membership.
known_pitfalls: joining layers in mismatched coordinate systems
double-assigning points that fall on a shared edge
dropping points that fall outside all boundaries silently
success_signals: each point maps to the boundary that contains it
points outside every boundary are reported, not dropped

blackbox.does: Checks a data processing request against recorded consent scope, purpose limitation, and retention windows, returning whether the processing is permitted and any expiry-driven obligations.

problem_solution.problem: Personal data gets processed for purposes beyond the consent given or held past its retention window, because no checkpoint ties processing to policy.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reuses data collected for one purpose in another flow and keeps it indefinitely, with no check of the consent scope or retention limit.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that evaluates a processing request against consent scope, purpose, and retention windows and returns a permit decision with obligations.
known_pitfalls: reusing data beyond the consented purpose
treating withdrawn consent as still valid
no obligation surfaced for expired data
success_signals: processing outside consent is denied
retention expiry raises an obligation
purpose limitation is enforced

blackbox.does: Classifies a content payload against declared safety categories and returns per-category labels with a policy action of allow, flag, or block, without altering the content.

problem_solution.problem: User and model content flows through with no safety classification, so disallowed categories reach users or downstream systems.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent blocks on a flat keyword list that both over-blocks ordinary text and misses obfuscated variants, with no per-category signal.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that classifies content against declared categories and returns per-category labels mapped to an allow, flag, or block action.
known_pitfalls: static thresholds with no policy control
success_signals: categories are labeled individually
the action follows the declared policy
content is returned unaltered

blackbox.does: Inspects an outbound payload and its destination against an egress policy, allowing, blocking, or requiring transformation when disallowed data or an unapproved destination is present.

problem_solution.problem: Data leaves a trust boundary to external destinations with no checkpoint, so regulated or internal-only data can be sent to an unapproved endpoint.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent forwards a full record to a third-party endpoint without checking classification or whether the destination is approved.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that evaluates outbound payload classification and destination against an egress policy before the data leaves the boundary.
known_pitfalls: checking destination but not payload contents
allowing an unapproved destination by default
success_signals: disallowed data or destinations are blocked
classification is evaluated per payload
blocked egress is recorded

blackbox.does: Matches resolved dependency versions against known vulnerability advisories and reports affected components with severity and a fixed-version reference under a declared policy.

problem_solution.problem: Known-vulnerable dependency versions ship in builds because nobody cross-checks the resolved versions against advisory data.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks only top-level versions, ignores version-range applicability, and treats every advisory as critical with no severity gating.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that matches resolved versions against advisories by affected range and reports affected components with severity and fixes.
known_pitfalls: no severity gating causing alert fatigue
stale advisory data missing recent entries
success_signals: affected components list a fixed version
severity gating is applied
transitive dependencies are evaluated

blackbox.does: Suspends a sensitive action pending explicit human approval, presenting the action context to an authorized approver and recording the decision and approver identity before proceeding.

problem_solution.problem: Sensitive or irreversible actions execute automatically, leaving no point for a human to review and authorize before the effect lands.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent proceeds with a high-impact action after a fabricated or implicit approval, with no record of who authorized it.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that pauses the action, presents context to an authorized approver, and proceeds only on a recorded explicit decision.
known_pitfalls: proceeding on timeout instead of denying
success_signals: the action waits for an explicit decision
the approver is authorized and recorded
denial or timeout blocks the action

blackbox.does: Resolves the declared license of each dependency and evaluates the set against an allow and deny policy, blocking the build when a disallowed or unknown license is present.

problem_solution.problem: Dependencies enter a codebase with copyleft or unknown licenses that conflict with the product's distribution terms, and the conflict is discovered only at release.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent adds a package for convenience without checking its license, or matches license names by loose string so a variant slips through.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that resolves each dependency license to a canonical identifier and gates the set against an allow and deny policy.
success_signals: disallowed licenses block the build
unknown licenses are flagged not ignored
transitive dependencies are covered

blackbox.does: Sanitizes generated output before it reaches a downstream sink by neutralizing active markup and redacting values that match sensitive or disallowed patterns under a declared policy.

problem_solution.problem: Model output is rendered or forwarded verbatim, so active markup or leaked sensitive values reach a browser, a shell, or a log.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts raw model output into an HTML page or a command, enabling injection, and forwards a response that still contains a secret.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that neutralizes active markup and redacts sensitive matches against the destination sink before output leaves the boundary.
known_pitfalls: redacting display text but not the underlying value
trusting output because the model is trusted
success_signals: active markup is neutralized for the target sink
sensitive matches are redacted
output is safe for the declared destination

blackbox.does: Detects personal, health, and cardholder data in a text payload, returning the matched spans with a category and a confidence signal, without modifying the source text.

problem_solution.problem: Free text flowing through a system may contain regulated personal, health, or cardholder data that must be identified before it is stored or forwarded.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent relies on a single loose regex that misses formatted card numbers and floods results with false positives on ordinary numbers.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that detects categorized sensitive spans with validation checks and a confidence signal, leaving the text unchanged.
known_pitfalls: no checksum validation for structured identifiers
ignoring data embedded in structured fields
success_signals: matched spans carry a category
structured identifiers pass checksum validation
source text is unchanged

blackbox.does: Redacts detected sensitive spans from a payload under a declared strategy such as masking, hashing, or tokenization, producing text that no longer contains the raw values.

problem_solution.problem: Sensitive values must be removed before text is logged, shared, or used for training, and partial or reversible redaction defeats the purpose.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent masks only the visible portion of a value, leaves the original in an adjacent field, or uses a reversible transform where irreversibility is required.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies the declared redaction strategy to detected spans so the output no longer carries the raw values.
known_pitfalls: original value surviving in another field
reversible transform where irreversible is required
breaking downstream parsing by changing length
success_signals: raw values are absent from the output
the chosen strategy matches the policy
a residual scan finds no leftover matches

blackbox.does: Evaluates a structured input against a declarative policy bundle and returns an allow or deny decision with the specific rules that fired, applying a default-deny stance.

problem_solution.problem: Authorization and admission rules are scattered across imperative code, so policy cannot be reviewed, tested, or changed independently of the application.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hardcodes if-branches for each rule, defaults to allow when no rule matches, and cannot explain which condition granted access.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that evaluates input against a declarative policy bundle with a default-deny stance and returns the rules that fired.
known_pitfalls: defaulting to allow on no match
policy and data drift out of sync
success_signals: no matching rule yields deny
the decision names the firing rules
policy is tested independently of the app

blackbox.does: Scans model input and retrieved context for instruction-override and exfiltration patterns and returns a risk verdict with the offending spans, without altering the input.

problem_solution.problem: Untrusted content pulled into a prompt can carry instructions that override the system policy or trigger data exfiltration.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent concatenates retrieved web or document text straight into the prompt with no screening, so embedded instructions are obeyed.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that screens input and retrieved context for override and exfiltration patterns and returns a risk verdict with spans.
known_pitfalls: screening only the user turn and not retrieved context
no separation of trusted and untrusted content
treating detection as a full defense on its own
success_signals: known injection patterns are flagged
offending spans are identified
trusted and untrusted content are distinguished

blackbox.does: Decides whether a request is within the allowed rate for its declared key using a defined limiting algorithm, returning an allow or throttle decision with the remaining budget.

problem_solution.problem: Endpoints and tools have no rate limiting, so a single caller can exhaust capacity or drive cost through unbounded request volume.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent limits on a coarse global counter, keys on a spoofable client field, and resets the window in a way that lets bursts through the boundary.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies a defined limiting algorithm per declared key and returns an allow or throttle decision with the remaining budget.
success_signals: requests over the limit are throttled
budget accounting is per key
a retry-after hint is returned

title: Software Bill of Materials Emit

blackbox.does: Emits a software bill of materials enumerating resolved components with versions, identifiers, and declared licenses in a standard interchange format for downstream analysis.

problem_solution.problem: When a new vulnerability lands there is no authoritative list of what components and versions a build actually contains, so impact cannot be assessed quickly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent lists only direct dependencies from a manifest, omitting transitive and system components and pinned versions, so the inventory is incomplete.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that enumerates resolved components with versions, package identifiers, and licenses in a standard SBOM format.
known_pitfalls: no versions so advisories cannot match
nonstandard format that tools cannot read
success_signals: transitive components are included
each component has an identifier and version
output validates against the standard schema

source_ref_families: NTIA Minimum Elements for an SBOM

blackbox.does: Validates a model-produced structured output against a declared schema and value constraints, returning a pass or a precise list of violations so an invalid result is never trusted.

problem_solution.problem: Structured output from a model is consumed as if it always matches the expected shape, so a malformed or out-of-range field crashes or corrupts downstream logic.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent parses the model output and accesses fields directly, assuming the schema holds, and passes an out-of-enum value straight into a database.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that validates the output against a schema and value constraints and returns a pass or a precise violation list.
known_pitfalls: checking types but not value ranges or enums
stopping at the first error instead of listing all
success_signals: invalid output is rejected with reasons
value constraints are enforced
every violation is reported

blackbox.does: Scans provided source content and diffs for high-entropy strings and known credential patterns, returning findings with location and rule while never emitting the matched secret value.

problem_solution.problem: Credentials get committed into source, and once pushed they are effectively exposed regardless of a later removal.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent commits a config file containing a live key, and a naive scanner echoes the matched secret into its own output or logs.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that scans content and diffs for credential patterns and high entropy, reporting findings by location without revealing the value.
known_pitfalls: echoing the matched secret in output
scanning only the working tree not history
entropy threshold too low causing noise
no allowance for verified test fixtures
success_signals: findings identify location and rule
the matched value never appears in output
diffs are scanned in addition to files

blackbox.does: Evaluates a model-proposed tool call against an allowlist and per-tool argument constraints, returning an allow or deny decision with a reason before any tool executes.

problem_solution.problem: Agents are wired to a broad set of tools with no gate, so a manipulated model can invoke a destructive or out-of-scope action directly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent framework executes whatever tool the model names with whatever arguments it supplies, trusting the model to stay in bounds.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that checks each proposed tool call against an allowlist and argument constraints and denies anything outside policy.
known_pitfalls: default allow instead of default deny
checking the tool name but not arguments
case or alias bypass of the allowlist
success_signals: calls outside the allowlist are denied
argument constraints are enforced
every decision carries a reason

blackbox.does: Converts an image between formats (PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF) with quality/compression policy, preserving or stripping metadata per request.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream tools require specific formats; ad hoc conversion loses quality or leaks metadata.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Re-encodes lossily by default or keeps EXIF that should be stripped.
problem_solution.solution: A format-convert primitive with explicit quality and metadata policy.
success_signals: target format produced
metadata handled per policy

blackbox.does: Crops an image into a batch of sub-images, one per bounding box, for per-object downstream processing.

problem_solution.problem: Per-object classification/OCR needs each detection cropped out of the source image.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Crops with wrong coordinate order or ignores clamping at image edges.
problem_solution.solution: A crop primitive that produces one sub-image per bbox, clamped to bounds.
success_signals: one crop per box
no out-of-bounds error

blackbox.does: Reads EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata from an image (capture time, geolocation, camera) into a normalized record.

problem_solution.problem: Photo pipelines need capture time and geolocation, which live in messy metadata blocks.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Ignores metadata or crashes on missing/oddly-encoded EXIF.
problem_solution.solution: A metadata-extract primitive returning a normalized record with graceful handling of missing fields.
success_signals: normalized record
missing fields null not error

blackbox.does: Resizes an image to a target size preserving aspect ratio (letterbox/crop per policy), recording the transform.

problem_solution.problem: Model inputs and thumbnails need consistent sizing without distortion.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Stretches to a fixed size, distorting aspect ratio.
problem_solution.solution: A resize primitive with aspect-preserving policy (letterbox or center-crop).
success_signals: output at requested size
aspect preserved per policy

blackbox.does: Tracks recent success and failure statistics for a downstream dependency and decides whether to allow, short-circuit, or probe a call based on the open, closed, or half-open state.

problem_solution.problem: When a downstream dependency degrades, callers keep hammering it, exhausting connections and amplifying the outage into their own service.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps calling a failing dependency on every request, piling up timeouts until the caller runs out of workers and fails too.
problem_solution.solution: A state machine that opens after a failure threshold to short-circuit calls, then half-opens to probe recovery before closing again.
known_pitfalls: breaker state not shared across instances
counting client errors as dependency failures
success_signals: calls short-circuit while the dependency is down
traffic resumes after recovery is probed

blackbox.does: Moves a message that has exhausted its processing attempts to a dead-letter destination with the failure reason and attempt metadata attached for later inspection.

problem_solution.problem: Messages that repeatedly fail either block the queue or vanish, and operators lose the context needed to diagnose why processing failed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent catches the error and drops the message, or retries it forever, so a poison message stalls the consumer or disappears with no trace.
problem_solution.solution: A routing capability that, after the attempt budget is spent, forwards the message plus failure metadata to a dead-letter destination and acknowledges the original.
known_pitfalls: infinite redelivery of a poison message
dropping the message with no record
success_signals: exhausted messages land in the dead-letter destination
failure context preserved
the primary queue is not blocked

blackbox.does: Wraps a payload in a standard event envelope carrying a unique id, type, source, timestamp, and content type so every emitted event shares one consistent metadata contract.

problem_solution.problem: Events emitted by different services carry inconsistent or missing metadata, so consumers cannot reliably deduplicate, trace, or route them.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent publishes the bare business payload with no id or type, forcing every consumer to invent its own correlation and routing scheme.
problem_solution.solution: An envelope wrapper that attaches a standard set of metadata fields around the payload following a common event-envelope contract.
known_pitfalls: putting business fields at the envelope level
success_signals: every event carries id, type, source, and time
consumers can deduplicate and route on metadata

blackbox.does: Validates an event against its registered schema and compatibility rules and reports whether it conforms and whether the producing version is compatible with consumers.

problem_solution.problem: Producers and consumers evolve independently, so an unvalidated schema change quietly breaks consumers that read a field that moved or changed type.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent publishes a changed event shape without checking compatibility, breaking every consumer that relied on the old contract.
problem_solution.solution: A validator that checks each event against its registered schema and enforces the declared compatibility policy before the event is accepted.
known_pitfalls: no pinned schema version on the event
success_signals: nonconforming events rejected
incompatible producer changes flagged before release

blackbox.does: Records a client-supplied idempotency key with the first result of a mutation and returns the stored result on any replay so a retried request applies its effect only once.

problem_solution.problem: Clients retry mutating requests after timeouts, and without an idempotency mechanism the same charge, order, or transfer is applied twice.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies the mutation on every call, or stores the key only after the effect, leaving a window where a concurrent retry double-applies.
problem_solution.solution: A key ledger that atomically reserves the key, records the first outcome, and short-circuits replays by returning the stored result.
known_pitfalls: recording the key after the side effect
reusing a key for a different request body
success_signals: retries return the original result
the effect is applied exactly once
mismatched bodies on the same key are rejected

blackbox.does: Delivers a signed event to a subscriber endpoint with retries and backoff, signing the body with the subscriber secret and recording the response for redelivery decisions.

problem_solution.problem: Emitting webhooks to third-party subscribers requires signing, retries, and delivery bookkeeping, and rolling this per integration produces unsigned or lost deliveries.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent posts the raw event once with no signature and no retry, so subscribers cannot authenticate it and a transient failure drops the event.
problem_solution.solution: A delivery capability that signs the payload with the subscriber secret, posts with bounded retries, and records each attempt for later redelivery.
known_pitfalls: no retry or backoff on transient failures
leaking the signing secret in logs
success_signals: subscribers can verify the signature
transient failures are retried
delivery attempts are auditable

blackbox.does: Checks a consumed queue message against its declared schema and envelope contract and reports structural or type violations before any handler processing begins.

problem_solution.problem: Malformed or version-skewed messages reach handlers that assume a shape, producing partial writes and cryptic failures deep inside processing.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent indexes fields off the message directly and lets a KeyError or type error surface halfway through a side-effecting handler.
problem_solution.solution: A gate that validates the message against its schema at the top of the consumer and routes structurally invalid messages away from business logic.
known_pitfalls: validating after side effects have started
no distinction between structural and business validation
success_signals: malformed messages rejected before handling
clear field-level violations reported

blackbox.does: Decides from the attempt count, elapsed time, and error class whether to retry and computes the next delay using bounded exponential backoff with jitter.

problem_solution.problem: Naive retry loops either give up too early or hammer a struggling dependency in lockstep, and every service hand-rolls its own delay math.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent retries in a tight loop with a fixed sleep and no cap, synchronizing thundering-herd retries and retrying non-retryable errors.
problem_solution.solution: A pure policy that classifies the error, enforces an attempt and deadline budget, and returns a capped exponential delay with jitter.
success_signals: delays stay within the configured ceiling
non-retryable errors stop immediately
budgets are respected

blackbox.does: Runs the declared compensating action that reverses the effect of a previously completed saga step when a later step fails, recording the outcome for the orchestrator.

problem_solution.problem: Multi-service workflows lack distributed transactions, so a failure partway through leaves earlier steps committed and the system in an inconsistent state.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent aborts the workflow without undoing completed steps, or writes ad hoc rollback code that is not idempotent and double-reverses on retry.
problem_solution.solution: A compensation executor that applies the declared inverse action for a completed step idempotently and reports the result to the saga orchestrator.
known_pitfalls: compensating a step that never committed
success_signals: completed steps are reversed exactly once
the workflow reaches a consistent terminal state

blackbox.does: Polls undelivered outbox rows, publishes each to the message broker, and marks it dispatched, retrying safely so a crash mid-batch never double-marks a row.

problem_solution.problem: The outbox pattern only works if a reliable relay drains pending events to the broker exactly as often as needed without duplicating or skipping rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent marks rows dispatched before the broker confirms, so a failed publish leaves a committed state change with no delivered event.
problem_solution.solution: A relay that publishes each pending row, marks it dispatched only after broker acknowledgement, and treats redelivery as at-least-once for consumers.
known_pitfalls: no ordering guarantee where consumers assume one
success_signals: every committed event is eventually delivered
rows are marked only after acknowledgement

blackbox.does: Persists an outgoing event into an outbox table inside the same database transaction as the business state change so the event and the state commit or roll back together.

problem_solution.problem: Writing to the database and publishing to a broker in two separate steps can leave the system with a committed state change but a lost event, or an emitted event for a rolled-back change.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent commits the row and then calls the broker afterward, so a crash between the two produces a state change no consumer ever hears about.
problem_solution.solution: An outbox writer that inserts the event row within the same transaction as the state change, deferring delivery to a separate dispatcher.
known_pitfalls: no dispatch-status column to drive the dispatcher
success_signals: event row commits atomically with the state change
no event exists for a rolled-back change

blackbox.does: Records each delivered event identifier in a durable store and reports whether an incoming delivery is a first-seen event or a duplicate redelivery within the retention window.

problem_solution.problem: Providers redeliver webhooks on timeout or retry, so handlers that assume exactly-once delivery double-process orders, charges, or state changes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent treats every delivery as new and processes side effects immediately, or keys dedupe on the payload hash so a legitimate repeat is silently dropped.
problem_solution.solution: A first-seen ledger keyed on the provider event identifier that classifies each delivery as new or duplicate before the handler runs.
