known_pitfalls: keying on payload hash instead of event id
no retention bound so the store grows unbounded
race between check and record under concurrency
success_signals: redeliveries classified as duplicates
first deliveries processed once
concurrent duplicates collapse to one

blackbox.does: Recomputes the expected signature over the raw request bytes with the shared secret and compares it in constant time against the header to decide whether an inbound webhook is authentic.

problem_solution.problem: Inbound webhooks are trivially spoofable unless every request is authenticated, yet each integration reimplements the signature check slightly differently and drifts.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent parses the JSON first and verifies over the re-serialized body, or uses an equality compare, so genuine requests fail and forged ones can slip through.
problem_solution.solution: A verifier that hashes the exact raw bytes with the signing secret and compares digests in constant time before any parsing, with a timestamp freshness window.
known_pitfalls: verifying over a parsed and re-serialized body
selecting the wrong secret or digest algorithm
success_signals: forged payloads rejected
genuine provider payloads accepted
stale replayed timestamps rejected

blackbox.does: Translates a provider-specific webhook payload into a normalized internal domain event with a stable type and field mapping, dropping vendor-only noise fields.

problem_solution.problem: Every downstream consumer ends up coupled to a vendor payload shape, so a provider schema change ripples through the whole system.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent passes the raw provider payload straight into business logic, spreading vendor field names and enum values across the codebase.
problem_solution.solution: A translation layer that maps the external payload onto a versioned internal domain-event schema at the boundary, isolating downstream code from the vendor shape.
known_pitfalls: silently dropping fields the mapping forgot
no versioning on the internal event
success_signals: downstream code depends only on the internal schema
vendor changes are absorbed at the boundary

blackbox.does: Concatenates an ordered set of video files into one, normalizing codecs/resolution so the join is seamless.

problem_solution.problem: Joining clips fails when codecs/resolutions differ, producing corrupt or stuttering output.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Byte-concatenates files with mismatched codecs.
problem_solution.solution: A concat primitive that normalizes codecs/resolution before joining in order.
success_signals: seamless single output
duration equals sum

blackbox.does: Downloads each URL in a set to files with bounded concurrency and per-item receipts, skipping items already present by checksum.

problem_solution.problem: Downloading a playlist means many downloads with retries, concurrency limits, and skip-if-present, done consistently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Loops sequentially with no concurrency cap, no retries, and re-downloads everything each run.
problem_solution.solution: A fan-out download over a URL set with bounded concurrency, retries, and checksum-based skipping.
success_signals: one file per requested item
failures isolated to their item

blackbox.does: Downloads a media URL to a local video file at a requested format/quality, recording the source URL, format, and checksum in a receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Bulk video download needs consistent format selection, resume, and provenance, which ad hoc scripts get wrong.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Re-downloads on every run and picks an unpredictable format, breaking downstream steps.
problem_solution.solution: A download primitive with explicit format policy, resume, and a receipt (source URL, format, checksum) for idempotent reuse.
success_signals: file present with expected format
checksum recorded
re-run is a no-op

blackbox.does: Expands a playlist or channel URL into the set of individual media item URLs, with per-item metadata, so downloads can fan out.

problem_solution.problem: Downloading 'a playlist' requires first resolving the ordered set of item URLs, which agents often hardcode or miss.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Assumes a fixed number of items or scrapes only the first page of a long playlist.
problem_solution.solution: A playlist expander that returns the complete ordered set of item URLs with pagination handled.
success_signals: item count matches source
order preserved

blackbox.does: Extracts the audio track from a video file to a requested codec/sample rate, recording the transcode parameters in a receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Transcription and audio analysis need the audio track pulled out at a known codec/sample rate.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Passes a whole video to an audio model, or extracts at the wrong sample rate for the downstream model.
problem_solution.solution: An audio-extract primitive with explicit codec/sample-rate policy and a receipt.
success_signals: audio file at requested codec/rate
duration matches source

blackbox.does: Samples frames from a video at a requested rate into an ordered frame sequence for per-frame vision processing.

problem_solution.problem: Per-frame vision (detection/tracking) needs frames sampled at a known rate with preserved order and timestamps.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Decodes every frame (huge) or loses frame timestamps/order.
problem_solution.solution: A frame-sampling primitive at a target FPS with ordered, timestamped output.
success_signals: frame count matches rate*duration
timestamps monotonic

blackbox.does: Fetches or extracts a subtitle/caption track for a media item in a requested language, returning cue-timed text.

problem_solution.problem: Existing captions are cheaper and often more accurate than re-transcribing, but tracks and languages vary.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Always re-transcribes even when an official caption track exists.
problem_solution.solution: A subtitle primitive that returns cue-timed text in the requested language when available.
success_signals: cue-timed text returned
language matches request

blackbox.does: Extracts a representative frame from a video and resizes it to a thumbnail at a requested size.

problem_solution.problem: Thumbnails need a representative frame at a consistent size, not the first black frame.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Grabs frame 0 (often black) or an arbitrary size.
problem_solution.solution: A thumbnail primitive that picks a representative frame and resizes to spec.
success_signals: non-blank thumbnail at requested size

blackbox.does: Resolves a media URL to its metadata (title, duration, formats, available streams) without downloading the media bytes.

problem_solution.problem: Agents download a whole video just to learn its title, length, or available formats, wasting bandwidth and time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Fetches full media bytes before checking whether the URL is valid or the format is available.
problem_solution.solution: A metadata-only resolve that returns title/duration/formats/streams for downstream planning.
success_signals: metadata returned without downloading bytes
format list non-empty

blackbox.does: Transcribes an audio file to timestamped text using a speech-to-text model, recording the model and language in a receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Turning media into searchable/analyzable text needs consistent, timestamped transcription with a recorded model.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: Runs a giant model on raw video, or loses timestamps and language metadata.
problem_solution.solution: A transcription primitive over extracted audio that emits timestamped segments and a model receipt.
success_signals: segments cover the duration
language recorded

blackbox.does: Creates a calendar event with attendees, time zone, and recurrence and issues invitations, returning a stable event identifier so later updates target the same event.

problem_solution.problem: Scheduling events across time zones and recurrence rules is error-prone, and re-running a create produces duplicate invitations to attendees.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent stores naive local times with no zone and creates a new event on every retry, spamming attendees with duplicate invites.
problem_solution.solution: A scheduling capability that encodes time zone and recurrence per the calendar standard and creates the event idempotently under a stable key.
known_pitfalls: storing times without a time zone
success_signals: events carry correct zone and recurrence
a retried create does not duplicate
updates target the same event id

blackbox.does: Produces a proposed reply to an email thread as an unsent draft, preserving quoting and threading headers and leaving the send decision to a human reviewer.

problem_solution.problem: Drafting contextual email replies at scale is repetitive, but auto-sending generated replies risks tone, factual, and privacy mistakes reaching recipients.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent generates a reply and sends it immediately, so a hallucinated commitment or leaked thread detail goes out with no review.
problem_solution.solution: A drafting capability that returns an unsent reply with correct threading and quoting for a human to review before sending.
success_signals: a reviewable draft is produced
threading headers are preserved
no send occurs without approval

blackbox.does: Submits a composed transactional email to the delivery provider with an idempotency key and returns the provider outcome and message identifier for tracking.

problem_solution.problem: Sending transactional email reliably means handling provider errors, retries, and duplicate sends without emailing the same user twice.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent posts to the provider and retries on any error with no idempotency key, sending duplicate emails when the first call actually succeeded.
problem_solution.solution: A send capability that submits with an idempotency key, classifies provider outcomes, and returns a trackable message identifier.
known_pitfalls: duplicate sends on retry without an idempotency key
success_signals: a retried send is not duplicated
provider outcome is captured
suppressed recipients are respected

blackbox.does: Renders an email template with merge data into HTML and text parts, escaping interpolated values so user-provided data cannot inject markup or break the layout.

problem_solution.problem: Email templates interpolate user data, and unescaped values break the layout or inject markup, while missing merge fields ship raw placeholders.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent concatenates data into the template without escaping and without checking that every required merge field is present, leaking placeholders or markup.
problem_solution.solution: A renderer that escapes interpolated values, validates required merge fields, and produces matched HTML and text parts.
success_signals: interpolated values are escaped
missing merge fields are caught before send
html and text parts match

blackbox.does: Creates a durable in-app notification record for a recipient with a type, payload, and unread status, coalescing repeats so a burst of identical events yields one entry.

problem_solution.problem: In-app notification feeds fill with duplicate entries when the same event fires repeatedly, and unread counts drift from the actual records.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts a new row for every event without coalescing, so a retried or repeated event floods the feed and inflates the unread count.
problem_solution.solution: A create capability that writes a typed notification record idempotently and coalesces repeats of the same event into a single entry.
known_pitfalls: duplicate feed entries on repeated events
success_signals: repeated events coalesce to one entry
unread counts match records
a retried create is a no-op

blackbox.does: Dispatches an approved newsletter campaign to a subscribed audience in resumable batches, skipping suppressed and unsubscribed recipients and recording per-recipient send status.

problem_solution.problem: A bulk campaign send must be resumable, must never re-send to someone twice, and must respect consent and suppression across a large audience.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent iterates the audience and sends in one pass with no checkpoint, so a mid-run crash re-sends to everyone already contacted on restart.
problem_solution.solution: A batched dispatcher that checkpoints progress, skips suppressed and unsubscribed recipients, and records per-recipient status so a resume never double-sends.
known_pitfalls: re-sending to already-contacted recipients on resume
sending to unsubscribed or suppressed addresses
no throttle against the provider rate limit
success_signals: each recipient is sent to at most once
unsubscribed and suppressed recipients are skipped
a crashed run resumes cleanly

blackbox.does: Assembles a dry-run preview of a newsletter campaign showing the resolved audience count, a rendered sample, and suppression exclusions without dispatching any message.

problem_solution.problem: Bulk newsletter sends are irreversible, and a mistaken audience filter or broken render reaches thousands before anyone notices.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent triggers the send directly to verify it works, dispatching a broken or mis-targeted campaign that cannot be recalled.
problem_solution.solution: A preview that resolves the audience and rendered sample and reports suppression exclusions as a reviewable artifact before any send.
known_pitfalls: triggering a real send to test
counting suppressed or unsubscribed recipients in the audience
previewing a different render than what would send
success_signals: audience and sample are reviewable before send
suppressed recipients are excluded
no message is dispatched

blackbox.does: Evaluates a notification intent against a user's channel preferences, consent, and quiet-hours settings to decide which channels may be used or that the notification must be suppressed.

problem_solution.problem: Users set channel preferences, consent, and quiet hours, but senders that ignore them message opted-out users and erode trust and compliance.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sends on every channel regardless of stored preferences, messaging users who opted out of a channel or category.
problem_solution.solution: A preference gate that intersects the intent with the user's consent, channel choices, and quiet hours to yield the allowed channels or a suppression.
known_pitfalls: defaulting to send when preferences are missing
success_signals: opted-out channels are excluded
quiet hours are honored
missing preferences default to the safe choice

blackbox.does: Delivers a push notification to registered device tokens through the platform gateway and reports per-token results, flagging invalid tokens for removal from the registry.

problem_solution.problem: Device tokens expire and rotate constantly, so pushing to a stale token registry wastes calls and leaves invalid tokens accumulating.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent pushes to every stored token and ignores the gateway's invalid-token responses, so dead tokens are never pruned and errors are lost.
problem_solution.solution: A send capability that delivers per token, records per-token results, and surfaces invalid tokens so the registry can prune them.
known_pitfalls: oversized payloads rejected by the gateway
success_signals: per-token outcomes are recorded
invalid tokens are flagged for removal

blackbox.does: Posts a formatted message to a chat channel through an incoming webhook, validating the block structure and returning the post outcome without leaking the webhook secret.

problem_solution.problem: Posting to a chat webhook seems trivial but the webhook URL is a secret, malformed blocks are rejected, and repeated triggers spam the channel.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes the webhook URL in source and posts unstructured text that the block schema rejects, or re-posts on every retry.
problem_solution.solution: A poster that validates the message block structure, submits through the injected webhook secret, and dedupes repeat posts by a client token.
known_pitfalls: embedding the webhook URL in source or logs
malformed message blocks rejected by the endpoint
success_signals: messages post with valid block structure
the webhook secret is not leaked
retries do not double-post

blackbox.does: Submits a text message to the SMS provider for a validated destination number, accounting for encoding and segment limits and returning the provider outcome and message identifier.

problem_solution.problem: SMS sending is metered per segment and requires valid numbers and consent, and naive sends miscount segments or message unreachable numbers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sends the raw string without normalizing the number or accounting for multi-byte encoding, splitting messages unexpectedly and failing on bad numbers.
problem_solution.solution: A send capability that validates and normalizes the destination number, computes segments from the encoding, and submits with an idempotency key.
success_signals: numbers are validated before send
segment count is computed correctly
retries are not duplicated

blackbox.does: Adds a signed one-click unsubscribe link and the required list and sender footer to an outbound bulk message so recipients can opt out through a standard mechanism.

problem_solution.problem: Bulk messages legally require a working unsubscribe path and sender identification, and messages missing them are non-compliant and get flagged as spam.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sends bulk mail with no unsubscribe link or with an unsigned link that anyone can forge to unsubscribe another user.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that injects a signed one-click unsubscribe link and the required footer following the list-unsubscribe conventions.
known_pitfalls: missing unsubscribe link on bulk mail
success_signals: every bulk message carries a working unsubscribe path
the unsubscribe token is signed and per-recipient

blackbox.does: Generates alerting rule definitions from a declared intent, attaching a for-duration to suppress flapping, a severity, and a runbook reference to each rule.

problem_solution.problem: Alerts fire on instantaneous spikes with no duration and no runbook, producing noise that on-call learns to ignore.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes an alert that triggers on a single scrape above a threshold, with no for-duration, no severity, and no link to a response procedure.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that generates rules with a suppression duration, a severity, and an attached runbook reference from a declared intent.
success_signals: rules include a suppression duration
each rule links a runbook
definitions validate against the schema

blackbox.does: Emits an append-only audit record capturing actor, action, target, and outcome with a trusted timestamp, in a form suited to tamper-evident retention and later review.

problem_solution.problem: Security-relevant actions are logged alongside debug noise with mutable, incomplete fields, so audit trails cannot answer who did what to which resource.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent logs an audit line as free text, omits the actor or the outcome, and mixes it into the same mutable stream as application logs.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that emits a complete append-only audit record with actor, action, target, outcome, and a trusted timestamp.
success_signals: records include actor, action, target, and outcome
the sink is append-only
timestamps are server-trusted

blackbox.does: Renders a dashboard definition from a declared set of panel intents, binding each panel to a query, a unit, and a layout position so the result is reproducible from source.

problem_solution.problem: Dashboards are clicked together by hand and drift from source control, so a panel breaks silently when a metric is renamed and nobody can rebuild it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-edits exported dashboard JSON, hardcodes a data source identifier, and leaves panels with no units or inconsistent time ranges.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders a reproducible dashboard from declared panel intents with bound queries, units, and layout.
success_signals: dashboard rebuilds from source
each panel binds a query and a unit
definition validates against the schema

blackbox.does: Verifies that an expected periodic heartbeat arrived within its allowed window and raises a verdict when a heartbeat is overdue, catching silent failures that emit no error.

problem_solution.problem: A scheduled job that stops running emits no error, so its silent absence goes unnoticed until downstream data is missing.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent only alerts on job failures, never on job absence, so a job that never starts produces no signal at all.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that treats a missing heartbeat within its window as the alarm condition, inverting failure detection to catch silence.
known_pitfalls: alerting only on failures not absence
grace window too tight causing false alarms
clock skew between emitter and checker
resetting the window on a late heartbeat
success_signals: a missing heartbeat raises a verdict
grace window absorbs jitter
silence is detected without an error event

blackbox.does: Reports aggregate service health by checking declared downstream dependencies within a bounded timeout and returning a structured status that distinguishes healthy, degraded, and unhealthy.

problem_solution.problem: Health endpoints return a static OK that ignores downstream dependencies, so orchestrators keep routing traffic to a service that cannot serve requests.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns two hundred unconditionally, or checks every dependency with no timeout so a slow dependency hangs the health check itself.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that probes declared dependencies within a bounded timeout and returns a structured healthy, degraded, or unhealthy status.
known_pitfalls: leaking internal details in the response
success_signals: status reflects dependency reality
checks respect the timeout
degraded and unhealthy are distinguished

blackbox.does: Renders a structured incident runbook from a declared context, laying out detection signals, triage steps, mitigation actions, and escalation contacts in a consistent order.

problem_solution.problem: Runbooks are inconsistent prose or missing entirely, so during an incident responders improvise the same triage from scratch every time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a vague paragraph with no concrete commands, no escalation path, and no link from the firing alert to the procedure.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that renders a structured runbook with detection, triage, mitigation, and escalation sections in a consistent layout.
known_pitfalls: runbook not linked from the alert
success_signals: sections follow a consistent layout
steps are concrete and actionable
escalation contacts are present

blackbox.does: Derives a numeric metric such as a count or a latency distribution from structured log records matching a declared filter, projecting selected fields into a bounded label set.

problem_solution.problem: Useful signals live only in logs, and re-querying full-text logs for a rate is slow and cannot feed alerting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent extracts a metric using a brittle substring match, promotes a high-cardinality field to a label, and double-counts on overlapping records.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that derives a count or distribution from filtered structured records with a bounded, validated label projection.
success_signals: metric derives deterministically from records
labels stay bounded
unparseable records are accounted for

blackbox.does: Records a counter, gauge, or histogram measurement under a stable metric name and a bounded label set, rejecting labels whose values would create unbounded cardinality.

problem_solution.problem: Metrics are emitted with high-cardinality labels like user or request identifiers, which overwhelms the time-series store and makes queries unusable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent adds a unique identifier as a metric label and mixes counters with gauges under the same name, corrupting aggregation.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that records a typed measurement under a stable name with a bounded, validated label set.
known_pitfalls: renaming a metric silently breaking dashboards
success_signals: labels stay within a bounded set
instrument type matches the measurement
names and units are stable

blackbox.does: Answers liveness and readiness probes separately, signaling whether the process should be restarted versus whether it is prepared to accept traffic, based on declared internal state.

problem_solution.problem: Liveness and readiness are conflated onto one check, so a warming instance gets killed as unhealthy or a broken instance keeps receiving traffic.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent points both the liveness and readiness probes at the same handler that also checks dependencies, causing restart loops when a dependency blips.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that separates a shallow liveness signal from a dependency-aware readiness signal with distinct semantics.
success_signals: warming instances are not restarted
unready instances are removed from traffic
liveness stays shallow

blackbox.does: Computes attainment against a service level objective over a rolling window and reports the remaining error budget and burn rate from a series of indicator samples.

problem_solution.problem: SLO attainment is eyeballed from dashboards, so teams cannot say how much error budget remains or how fast it is burning.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent averages availability over the wrong window, counts maintenance windows against the budget, and confuses attainment with burn rate.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that computes attainment, remaining budget, and burn rate over the declared rolling window from indicator samples.
known_pitfalls: counting excluded time against the budget
gaps in the series skewing the result
success_signals: remaining budget is explicit
burn rate is reported separately
excluded windows are honored

blackbox.does: Emits a single structured log event as one machine-parseable record with a stable level, timestamp, and correlation fields, dropping or masking fields flagged as sensitive.

problem_solution.problem: Logs are free-form strings that cannot be queried, and correlation identifiers and sensitive values are scattered inconsistently across messages.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent formats logs with string concatenation, omits a request identifier, and prints a full request body that includes a token.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that emits one structured record per event with stable fields and correlation identifiers, masking flagged sensitive fields.
success_signals: every record is machine-parseable
correlation fields are present
flagged fields are masked

blackbox.does: Opens and closes a trace span around an operation, propagating parent context, attaching attributes, and recording the span status even when the wrapped operation raises.

problem_solution.problem: Spans are started but never closed on the error path, and context is not propagated across boundaries, so traces are broken and orphaned.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent starts a span, and an exception skips the close call, leaking the span and losing the error status while dropping the parent link.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that brackets an operation with a span, propagates parent context, and closes with a recorded status on every path.
known_pitfalls: lost parent context across a boundary
success_signals: spans close on every path
parent context is preserved
error status is recorded

blackbox.does: Checks that every citation in an answer resolves to a real retrieved chunk and that the cited chunk actually supports the statement it is attached to, returning per-citation verdicts.

problem_solution.problem: Citations can point at the wrong chunk or a chunk that does not support the claim, so their correctness must be checked rather than assumed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts that a present citation is a correct one, letting mislinked or unsupported citations pass unchecked.
problem_solution.solution: A citation-validation capability that resolves each citation to its chunk and confirms the chunk supports the cited statement.
known_pitfalls: accepting a citation that resolves but does not support the claim
citations referencing chunks outside the retrieved set
passing an answer with unsupported statements
success_signals: citations that do not support their statement fail validation
every citation resolves to a chunk in the retrieved set

blackbox.does: Attaches citations to the parts of an answer that draw on retrieved chunks, linking each cited span of the answer to the chunk reference that supports it.

problem_solution.problem: An answer built from retrieved chunks is only auditable if each supported statement carries a citation back to the chunk it used.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends a flat list of sources at the end, so no reader can tell which sentence rests on which chunk.
problem_solution.solution: A citation capability that links each supported span of the answer to the specific chunk reference behind it.
known_pitfalls: citing a chunk the span does not actually use
one bucket of sources with no span alignment
citations pointing at chunks not in the retrieved set
success_signals: each cited span links to a chunk in the retrieved set
supported statements carry a citation

blackbox.does: Turns text items into fixed-length embedding vectors with a declared model, returning the vectors tied to their item ids and the model identity that produced them.

problem_solution.problem: Semantic retrieval needs vectors, and mixing embeddings from different models or dimensions silently breaks the index they land in.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent embeds with whatever model is handy and never records which one, so vectors from two models get compared as if compatible.
problem_solution.solution: An embedding capability that produces fixed-length vectors under a declared model and records the model identity with the output.
known_pitfalls: mixing vectors from different models in one index
success_signals: every vector carries the model identity that produced it
all vectors in one output share the same dimension

blackbox.does: Scores a retrieval or answer run against a labeled evaluation set with declared metrics and returns the per-metric results and the sample size they were computed over.

problem_solution.problem: Retrieval and answer quality can only be tracked if a run is scored against a fixed labeled set with declared, reproducible metrics.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent eyeballs a few answers and declares the system improved, with no metric, no labeled set, and no reproducible number.
problem_solution.solution: An eval-scoring capability that computes declared metrics over a labeled set and reports the results with the sample size behind them.
known_pitfalls: scoring on a different slice than last time and comparing anyway
reporting a metric with no sample size
leaking labels into the run being evaluated
success_signals: the same run and label set reproduce the same scores
every metric is reported with its sample size

blackbox.does: Assesses whether each claim in an answer is supported by the supplied evidence and flags statements that go beyond it, returning a faithfulness verdict with the unsupported claims listed.

problem_solution.problem: A grounded-looking answer can still contain claims the evidence never supports, and those unsupported claims must be caught before the answer is trusted.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent ships the answer because it cites sources, without checking whether each claim is actually entailed by them.
problem_solution.solution: A faithfulness-checking capability that tests each claim against the evidence and flags statements that exceed what the evidence supports.
known_pitfalls: passing an answer whose extra claims have no evidence
checking the answer as a whole rather than per claim
confusing fluent phrasing with grounded support
success_signals: claims beyond the evidence are flagged
the verdict lists the specific unsupported statements

blackbox.does: Reorders a candidate chunk set for a query with a relevance model and returns the reranked list preserving each chunk's reference so citations still resolve.

problem_solution.problem: First-stage retrieval ranks by vector similarity alone, which often puts a more relevant chunk below a less relevant one for the query.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent feeds the first-stage order straight to the answer step, or reranks but loses the chunk references in the process.
problem_solution.solution: A reranking capability that scores each candidate against the query with a relevance model and reorders while keeping references intact.
known_pitfalls: reranking more candidates than the model can handle
reintroducing chunks that retrieval already filtered out
success_signals: chunk references survive the rerank
the reranked order reflects the relevance scores

blackbox.does: Searches a vector index for the nearest chunks to a query and returns a ranked list with the similarity scores and chunk references needed to cite them.

problem_solution.problem: Answering over a corpus needs the most relevant chunks for a query, returned with scores and references so the answer can be grounded.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns chunk text with no scores or ids, so later stages cannot rerank, cite, or trace the retrieval.
problem_solution.solution: A retrieval capability that queries the vector index and returns ranked chunks with similarity scores and stable references.
known_pitfalls: querying with a metric the index was not built for
silently truncating below the requested top-k
success_signals: results carry scores and references for every chunk
the query metric matches the index metric

blackbox.does: Splits source text into retrieval chunks under a declared size and overlap policy, keeping each chunk tied to its document and character offsets for later citation.

problem_solution.problem: Retrieval works on chunks, and poor chunking either splits an idea across boundaries or builds chunks too large to retrieve precisely.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-splits on a fixed character count with no overlap or offsets, orphaning sentences and losing citation anchors.
problem_solution.solution: A chunking capability that applies a declared size and overlap policy and keeps each chunk anchored to its document offsets.
known_pitfalls: overlap so large that chunks duplicate content
dropping offsets needed for later citation
success_signals: each chunk maps back to its document offsets
the same text and policy chunk identically

blackbox.does: Builds a searchable vector index from a set of embeddings under a declared index configuration and persists it with the metric and parameters needed to query it correctly.

problem_solution.problem: Retrieval needs a persisted vector index, and an index built with the wrong metric or mismatched dimension returns quietly wrong neighbors.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds an index without recording its metric or parameters, so queries later use a distance the index was never built for.
problem_solution.solution: An index-build capability that constructs and persists a vector index together with the metric and parameters required to query it.
known_pitfalls: query metric disagreeing with the build metric
adding vectors of a different dimension
rebuilds that are not reproducible from the same inputs
success_signals: the persisted index records its metric and parameters
rebuilding from the same embeddings yields an equivalent index

blackbox.does: Evaluates attribute-based access policies over subject, resource, action, and environment attributes and returns a decision with the obligations that apply.

problem_solution.problem: Attribute-based rules are expressive but easy to write with conflicting or overly broad conditions that silently over-grant.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-codes nested conditionals per endpoint, produces conflicting rules, and lacks a defined combining rule so results are inconsistent.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that evaluates a declared policy set with an explicit combining algorithm and default-deny, surfacing obligations alongside the decision.
known_pitfalls: conflicting rules with no combining algorithm
success_signals: deterministic decisions
default-deny on missing attributes
obligations returned with the decision

blackbox.does: Generates a high-entropy API key bound to a principal and scopes, returning the secret once and persisting only a hashed verifier with metadata.

problem_solution.problem: API keys are often stored in plaintext, unscoped, and impossible to attribute or expire once issued.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent stores the raw key string in a column and returns it on later reads, so a database read exposes every caller's key.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that mints a high-entropy key, shows it once, and stores only a hash plus scope, owner, and lifetime metadata.
known_pitfalls: key not attributable to an owner
success_signals: only a hash is stored
key revealed once
scope and owner recorded

blackbox.does: Immediately invalidates an API key so subsequent presentations are rejected, and records the revocation reason for audit.

problem_solution.problem: When a key leaks it must stop working instantly, but revocation is often eventual or missing entirely.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent removes the key only from a cache and lets the database copy keep validating, so the leaked key still works.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that writes an authoritative revocation checked on every verification path and takes effect immediately and idempotently.
success_signals: revoked key rejected immediately
repeat revoke is a no-op
reason captured for audit

blackbox.does: Issues a replacement API key for an existing binding with an overlap window during which both keys work, then retires the superseded key.

problem_solution.problem: Rotation that instantly invalidates the old key causes outages, so teams avoid rotating and keys live indefinitely.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent swaps the key in place with no overlap window, breaking every live integration the moment it rotates.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that issues a new key alongside the old one for a bounded overlap window and retires the superseded key on schedule.
known_pitfalls: losing owner and scope on rotation
success_signals: new and old keys both work during overlap
old key retired on schedule
scope and owner preserved

blackbox.does: Records a structured, tamper-evident audit event for a security-relevant action with actor, action, target, and outcome fields to an append-only sink.

problem_solution.problem: Security investigations fail because audit events are inconsistent, mutable, or missing the who, what, and outcome.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes free-text log lines with varying fields to a mutable store, so events cannot be correlated or trusted after the fact.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that emits a schema-constrained, append-only audit record with a stable actor-action-target-outcome shape and correlation id.
success_signals: events share a stable schema
records are append-only
actions are attributable and correlated

blackbox.does: Confirms that a state-changing request carries a valid anti-forgery token bound to the caller's session before the action is allowed to proceed.

problem_solution.problem: Browser state-changing endpoints are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery when they rely only on ambient cookies.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent authorizes a mutation purely on the session cookie, so any site can forge the request on the user's behalf.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that requires and validates a per-session anti-forgery token in constant time, matching it against the bound session on every mutation.
known_pitfalls: token not bound to the session
success_signals: forged cross-site requests rejected
token bound to the session
safe methods handled correctly

blackbox.does: Applies a retention policy to a data scope by identifying records past their retention window and expiring, anonymizing, or archiving them per policy.

problem_solution.problem: Data is kept indefinitely because retention rules are documented but never enforced against the actual stores.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a one-off delete script with no dry run, no idempotency, and no record of what it removed, risking over-deletion.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that selects records past their retention window and expires, anonymizes, or archives them idempotently with a dry-run mode and an outcome log.
core_components: expire or anonymize or archive action
known_pitfalls: over-deleting due to a wrong window
no dry run before destructive action
success_signals: only past-window records affected
reruns are idempotent
legal holds are respected

blackbox.does: Executes a tracked erasure across all systems holding a subject's data, honoring legal holds and recording per-system completion for the deletion ticket.

problem_solution.problem: Honoring a deletion request means erasing data from primary stores, backups, caches, and downstreams, which is easy to do partially.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes from the main table and calls it done, leaving copies in caches, search indexes, and analytics, so data persists.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that fans erasure out to every registered store for the subject, tracks per-system completion, and honors legal holds and exemptions.
success_signals: all registered stores erased or exempted
completion tracked per system
legal holds respected

blackbox.does: Encrypts and decrypts individual sensitive field values under a managed key with authenticated encryption, tagging each ciphertext with the key version used.

problem_solution.problem: Sensitive fields are stored in plaintext or encrypted without authentication or key-version tracking, blocking rotation and tamper detection.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent encrypts with an unauthenticated mode and a hard-coded key, so ciphertext can be tampered with and keys can never rotate.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies authenticated encryption under a versioned managed key and decrypts by the key version tagged on each ciphertext.
success_signals: ciphertext is authenticated
decryption follows the tagged key version
keys can be rotated

blackbox.does: Encodes or strips untrusted content for a specific output context so that embedded markup or control sequences cannot execute where it is rendered.

problem_solution.problem: Reflecting user content into HTML, SQL, shell, or logs without context-correct encoding causes injection and cross-site scripting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies one blanket escape or a denylist of tags, which misses the actual output context and is bypassed by encoding tricks.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies context-specific output encoding for the exact sink, defaulting to escape rather than filter.
success_signals: content is inert in its sink
context-correct encoding applied
injection payloads neutralized

blackbox.does: Derives a salted, slow, one-way verifier from a plaintext secret and checks a candidate secret against a stored verifier without revealing it.

problem_solution.problem: Passwords are still stored with fast or unsalted hashes, or with home-grown schemes that are trivial to reverse at scale.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hashes passwords with a fast general-purpose digest and no salt or work factor, making offline cracking cheap.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies a salted, adaptive, slow key-derivation function with a tunable work factor and constant-time verification.
success_signals: verifier is salted and slow
work factor is tunable
verification is constant-time

blackbox.does: Compiles the effective subject-by-resource permission matrix from the role and policy model so access can be reviewed and diffed as data.

problem_solution.problem: Nobody can answer who can do what because effective permissions are spread across roles, groups, and inline rules.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent eyeballs role definitions and misses inherited or wildcard grants, so the review misses real effective access.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that resolves inheritance and wildcards into a flat, reviewable matrix of effective permissions for audit and diffing.
success_signals: effective access is fully enumerated
output is stable and diffable
reviewers can spot over-grants

blackbox.does: Assembles a verified subject's personal data from across systems into a portable, structured export packet that includes only that subject's records.

problem_solution.problem: Subject access and portability requests require gathering personal data from many systems without leaking other people's data.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent dumps a broad query that includes records belonging to other subjects and ships it without verifying the requester.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that verifies the request, collects only the subject's records across sources, and packages them in a portable, documented format.
known_pitfalls: exporting derived secrets or internal fields
success_signals: packet contains only the subject's data
all in-scope sources covered
requester was verified

blackbox.does: Accounts a request against a keyed quota window and returns an allow or throttle decision with the remaining budget and a retry hint.

problem_solution.problem: Without shared rate limiting, brute-force and abuse traffic overwhelms endpoints and per-instance counters diverge.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps an in-memory counter per process, so limits reset on deploy and do not hold across replicas.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that accounts requests against a shared keyed window and returns a consistent allow or throttle decision with a retry hint.
known_pitfalls: keying on a spoofable client ip only
success_signals: limits hold across replicas
abusive keys throttled
clients receive a retry hint

blackbox.does: Grants or removes a role for a subject within a scope, enforcing that the actor may delegate that role and recording the binding change for audit.

problem_solution.problem: Role assignment without delegation checks lets users grant themselves or others privileges they do not hold.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a role binding directly from a request without checking whether the actor is allowed to grant that role, enabling privilege escalation.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that verifies the actor can delegate the target role in the target scope before writing the binding and logs every change.
known_pitfalls: granting a role the actor lacks
success_signals: only delegable roles can be granted
scope is enforced
every change is logged

blackbox.does: Decides whether a subject holding a set of roles may perform an action on a resource type, returning an allow or deny with the deciding role path.

problem_solution.problem: Authorization checks scattered through handlers drift apart and default to allow when a role or mapping is missing.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inlines role string comparisons per route, misses some paths, and treats an unknown role as permitted, opening access holes.
problem_solution.solution: A single evaluator that resolves roles to permissions against one model and denies by default when no grant matches.
success_signals: unmatched requests denied
one evaluator used everywhere
decisions are explainable

blackbox.does: Validates and coerces an inbound request payload against a declared schema, rejecting unknown fields and out-of-range values before business logic runs.

problem_solution.problem: Handlers that trust request bodies are exposed to injection, mass assignment, and type-confusion bugs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads fields off the raw body with permissive parsing and no allowlist, so unexpected fields and types reach the core logic.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that enforces a strict schema at the boundary, rejecting unknown fields and coercing only within declared bounds.
success_signals: malformed payloads rejected at the edge
unknown fields dropped or refused
errors are structured

blackbox.does: Verifies that the acting subject owns or is explicitly granted the specific object being accessed, closing insecure direct object reference gaps.

problem_solution.problem: Object-level authorization is missed constantly, so changing an id in a request exposes another user's record.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks that the user is logged in but not that they own the requested object, so incrementing an id returns someone else's data.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that resolves the object's owner or grant list and confirms the subject is authorized for that specific instance before access.
success_signals: non-owners denied per object
id tampering yields denial
checks applied on nested paths

blackbox.does: Detects and masks credentials, tokens, and other sensitive values in text or structured payloads before they are logged, displayed, or exported.

problem_solution.problem: Secrets leak into logs, error messages, and exports because redaction is applied inconsistently or not at all.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent logs whole request objects and stack traces, spilling tokens and passwords into log stores that are widely readable.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that detects known secret shapes and sensitive keys and masks them consistently across text and structured content at the boundary.
known_pitfalls: partial masking that still reveals the secret
success_signals: secrets masked in logs and exports
nested fields covered
no full secret survives redaction

blackbox.does: Scans code, configuration, and history for committed credentials and high-entropy secrets and reports located findings for triage and rotation.

problem_solution.problem: Secrets get committed to repositories and configuration and stay there through history long after the file changes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent greps for the word password and misses real high-entropy tokens and secrets buried in version history.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies pattern and entropy detection across the working tree and history and reports each finding with its location.
known_pitfalls: scanning only the current tree not history
secrets in binary or encoded blobs
success_signals: committed secrets located with paths
history is covered
findings are actionable for rotation

blackbox.does: Adds and normalizes the response security headers a policy requires, such as content security, transport security, and framing controls, without dropping existing safe values.

problem_solution.problem: Responses ship without hardening headers or with inconsistent ones, leaving clickjacking, mixed-content, and sniffing gaps.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sets headers ad hoc per route, forgets some responses, and ships an overly permissive content security policy.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that applies the policy's header set uniformly to every response and flags weak or missing directives.
success_signals: required headers present on every response
weak directives flagged
policy applied consistently

blackbox.does: Creates a non-human service identity with least-privilege scopes and bounded credential lifetime, returning credentials once and storing only their verifier.

problem_solution.problem: Service accounts are routinely over-privileged, share long-lived static secrets, and are never rotated or inventoried.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent creates a broad admin service account with a permanent secret and hard-codes it, giving one leak full access indefinitely.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that provisions a scoped service identity with a bounded-lifetime credential, returned once and stored only as a verifier.
success_signals: least-privilege scopes assigned
credential shown once only
identity is inventoried and owned

blackbox.does: Enforces that every data access carries and matches the resolved tenant scope, blocking cross-tenant reads and writes at the access boundary.

problem_solution.problem: Cross-tenant data leakage happens when a query forgets its tenant filter or an object id from one tenant is used in another.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent relies on each query author to remember the tenant filter, so one missing where clause leaks another tenant's rows.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that requires the tenant scope on every access and rejects any object whose owning tenant does not match the caller's scope.
known_pitfalls: missing tenant filter on a query
success_signals: cross-tenant access blocked
every access carries a scope
violations are logged

blackbox.does: Determines the authoritative tenant scope for a request from verified context and rejects ambiguous or spoofable tenant hints before any data access.

problem_solution.problem: Multi-tenant systems often infer the tenant from a client-supplied header that an attacker can change to reach another tenant.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads a tenant id from a request header or body and trusts it, letting a caller pivot into another tenant by editing the value.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that derives the tenant only from verified, server-trusted context and refuses requests with missing or conflicting tenant signals.
success_signals: tenant derived from trusted context only
spoofed hints rejected
scope resolved before any query

blackbox.does: Produces a signed, integrity-protected token from a claim set with bounded lifetime, audience, and issuer fields under an active signing key.

problem_solution.problem: Signed tokens are issued with no expiry, no audience, or an algorithm that a verifier can be tricked into downgrading.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent signs a token with a fixed key, no expiry, and an algorithm field the client controls, enabling long-lived or downgraded tokens.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that signs claims with a pinned algorithm and active key, always setting bounded lifetime, audience, and issuer.
success_signals: tokens carry bounded lifetime and audience
algorithm is pinned
key id is recorded for rotation

blackbox.does: Verifies a presented token's signature, algorithm, expiry, audience, and issuer against policy and returns the trusted claims only when all checks pass.

problem_solution.problem: Token verification frequently trusts the token's own algorithm header or skips audience and expiry checks, accepting forged tokens.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent decodes a token and reads its claims without verifying the signature or honoring the none algorithm, trusting attacker-controlled data.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that pins accepted algorithms, verifies the signature against the expected key, and enforces expiry, audience, and issuer before returning claims.
success_signals: forged or expired tokens rejected
only pinned algorithms accepted
claims returned only after full verification

blackbox.does: Recommends an approximate-nearest-neighbor index type and parameters for a described workload, reporting the tradeoffs behind the choice without building the index itself.

problem_solution.problem: Choosing an approximate-nearest-neighbor index is a tradeoff among recall, memory, and build cost that depends on the workload, and a blind default often misfits it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent always reaches for the same index type regardless of vector count, dimension, or recall need, and cannot explain the choice.
problem_solution.solution: An index-selection capability that maps a described workload to an index type and parameters and reports the tradeoffs behind the recommendation.
known_pitfalls: recommending an index that ignores the recall target
suggesting parameters that exceed the memory budget
a recommendation with no stated tradeoffs
success_signals: the recommendation states its recall and resource tradeoffs
the same workload profile yields the same recommendation

blackbox.does: Reduces a candidate pair set to a smaller high-recall subset using a similarity or blocking rule and reports the reduction ratio and the pairs it dropped.

problem_solution.problem: A candidate pair set can still be too large to score, so it must be reduced without quietly discarding the true matches it is meant to preserve.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trims the pair set with an aggressive rule and never measures how many true matches it just dropped.
problem_solution.solution: A blocking-reduction capability that shrinks the pair set under a declared rule and reports the reduction ratio and the discarded pairs.
known_pitfalls: reducing so hard that true matches are lost
reporting a reduced set with no reduction ratio
an unstable rule that keeps different pairs each run
success_signals: the reduced set reports its reduction ratio
discarded pairs are recorded, not silently dropped

blackbox.does: Computes cosine similarity or distance between two vectors under a declared normalization convention, reporting the convention so scores stay comparable across callers.

problem_solution.problem: Vector comparison needs a single agreed cosine convention, since mixing similarity and distance or normalized and raw vectors makes scores incomparable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes cosine one way here and another way there, then compares the two numbers as if they meant the same thing.
problem_solution.solution: A cosine capability that computes the score under a declared similarity-or-distance and normalization convention and reports which convention it used.
known_pitfalls: undefined score on a zero vector
success_signals: identical vectors score at the convention's maximum similarity
the reported convention matches how the score was computed

blackbox.does: Computes the great-circle distance between two latitude and longitude coordinates on a spherical earth model and reports the distance in the declared unit.

problem_solution.problem: Distance between geographic coordinates cannot use planar math, and results are meaningless unless the unit is stated.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent subtracts latitude and longitude and treats the result as distance, producing values that grow wrong toward the poles.
problem_solution.solution: A haversine capability that computes great-circle distance on a spherical model and reports the distance in a declared unit.
known_pitfalls: applying planar distance to geographic coordinates
reporting a distance without its unit
success_signals: identical coordinates have zero distance
the reported unit matches the returned magnitude

blackbox.does: Computes the Jaccard similarity or distance between two sets as the ratio of their intersection to their union, defining the result explicitly when both sets are empty.

problem_solution.problem: Set overlap comparison needs a consistent Jaccard definition, including a defined answer for the empty-set edge case that otherwise divides by zero.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes intersection over union without handling two empty sets, throwing or returning an undefined value on that case.
problem_solution.solution: A Jaccard capability that computes intersection over union under a declared convention and defines the empty-empty case explicitly.
known_pitfalls: dividing by zero on two empty sets
counting duplicate elements when sets are expected
success_signals: identical sets score at maximum similarity
the empty-empty case returns the declared defined value

blackbox.does: Computes the edit distance between two strings as the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions, optionally normalized by length.

problem_solution.problem: Fuzzy string comparison needs a consistent edit-distance definition, and mixing raw and length-normalized distances makes thresholds meaningless.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent thresholds raw edit distance across strings of very different lengths, so the same threshold means different things per pair.
problem_solution.solution: An edit-distance capability that computes insertions, deletions, and substitutions and reports whether the result is raw or length-normalized.
known_pitfalls: comparing raw distances across very different lengths
counting code units rather than characters on wide scripts
mixing raw and normalized results under one threshold
success_signals: identical strings have zero edit distance
the reported convention matches how distance was computed

blackbox.does: Builds a locality-sensitive hashing index over MinHash signatures so that near-duplicate candidates can be looked up by band, recording the band and row configuration used.

problem_solution.problem: Even with signatures, comparing every pair is too much, so near-duplicate candidates must be retrievable without scanning the whole corpus.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent still loops over all signature pairs, or builds an LSH index without recording its band configuration so recall cannot be reasoned about.
problem_solution.solution: An LSH-index capability that hashes signatures into bands and persists the index with the band and row configuration that governs its recall.
known_pitfalls: a band configuration that misses true near-duplicates
mixing signatures of different lengths into one index
rebuilds that are not reproducible from the same signatures
success_signals: the index records its band and row configuration
candidate lookups return signatures sharing a band

blackbox.does: Builds a fixed-length MinHash signature from a token set so that set similarity can be estimated by comparing signatures, recording the hash family and permutation count used.

problem_solution.problem: Comparing large sets pairwise is expensive, and estimating their similarity needs compact signatures built the same way for every set.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds signatures with different permutation counts or hash families and then compares them as if they were compatible.
problem_solution.solution: A MinHash capability that produces a fixed-length signature under a declared hash family and permutation count and records both.
known_pitfalls: changing the hash family between signatures
seeding permutations differently across a corpus
success_signals: the same token set and config yield the same signature
signatures across the corpus share length and hash family

blackbox.does: Measures recall at one or more cutoffs by comparing retrieved neighbors against a labeled relevant set and reports the per-cutoff recall with the query count behind it.

problem_solution.problem: An index or retriever can only be compared if its recall at fixed cutoffs is measured against a labeled relevant set in a reproducible way.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent spot-checks a few queries and asserts recall improved, with no cutoff, no labeled set, and no reproducible number.
problem_solution.solution: A recall-at-k capability that compares retrieved neighbors to labeled relevant items at declared cutoffs and reports recall with the query count.
known_pitfalls: reporting recall with no cutoff attached
averaging over a different query slice than before
counting a near-duplicate as a distinct relevant hit
success_signals: each recall number states its cutoff and query count
the same retrieval and labels reproduce the same recall

blackbox.does: Produces a SimHash fingerprint from weighted features so that near-duplicate documents can be compared by the Hamming distance between fingerprints, recording the bit width used.

problem_solution.problem: Near-duplicate detection over documents needs a compact fingerprint whose bit differences track content differences in a consistent way.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares fingerprints of different bit widths or built from different feature weightings, so Hamming distances are not comparable.
problem_solution.solution: A SimHash capability that folds weighted features into a fixed-width fingerprint and records the bit width so distances stay comparable.
known_pitfalls: comparing fingerprints of different bit widths
treating Hamming distance as an exact similarity
success_signals: identical feature vectors yield identical fingerprints
fingerprints across the corpus share the recorded bit width

blackbox.does: Returns a paginated, access-filtered activity feed for an actor or entity, merging events from tracked sources into one reverse-chronological, cursor-paged view.

problem_solution.problem: An activity feed merges events from several trackers and must page stably and hide events the viewer may not see, or it leaks activity and drifts under new events.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent concatenates event tables and offset-paginates without visibility filtering, leaking others' activity and repeating rows as new events arrive.
problem_solution.solution: A feed-read capability that merges tracked event sources, applies per-viewer visibility, and pages by a stable cursor in reverse-chronological order.
known_pitfalls: leaking events the viewer cannot see
offset paging repeating or skipping events
success_signals: feed shows only viewer-visible events
cursor paging is stable under new events

blackbox.does: Validates a product analytics event against a tracking plan and appends it to the event store with identity and timestamp, deduplicating by a client-supplied event id.

problem_solution.problem: Product analytics is only trustworthy if events conform to a tracking plan and are counted once, but ad hoc event capture drifts in schema and double-counts.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent accepts arbitrary event shapes and re-ingests retried events, so property names drift and metrics inflate from duplicates.
problem_solution.solution: An event-track capability that validates each event against the tracking plan, stamps identity and time, and deduplicates by a client event id.
known_pitfalls: personal data captured in event properties
success_signals: events conform to the tracking plan
the same client event id is stored once

blackbox.does: Records an asset's custody, location, and condition changes across its lifecycle, appending each assignment or status change to a chain-of-custody trail.

problem_solution.problem: Assets change custody, location, and condition over their life, and losing the chain of custody makes loss, audit, and depreciation tracking unreliable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reassigns an asset's holder without recording the prior custodian, breaking the chain of custody and hiding who last had it.
problem_solution.solution: An asset-tracker capability that validates the custody or status change, records location and condition, and appends a chain-of-custody entry.
known_pitfalls: retired asset still shown as in service
success_signals: chain of custody is continuous and ordered
retirement reflected in the asset status

blackbox.does: Updates a case's status, assignment, and linked parties across an investigation or service workflow, appending each action to an access-controlled case file.

problem_solution.problem: Cases carry sensitive party information and require a defensible action trail, so status and assignment changes must be recorded and access-scoped.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent changes case status and reassigns it without recording who acted or why, weakening the defensibility of the case file.
problem_solution.solution: A case-tracker capability that validates the workflow transition, updates assignment and parties, and appends an access-controlled case-file entry.
known_pitfalls: actions recorded without actor or reason
party information exposed to unauthorized readers
closed case reopened without an audit entry
success_signals: every action attributed in the case file
case file readable only by authorized roles

blackbox.does: Moves a claim through submitted, under-review, approved, denied, and paid states, recording adjudication decisions and amounts and appending each decision event.

problem_solution.problem: Claim adjudication has financial and regulatory consequences, so each state change and amount must be recorded with its decision basis and never silently revised.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sets a claim to paid without recording the approved amount and decision basis, leaving the payout unexplained and un-auditable.
problem_solution.solution: A claim-tracker capability that validates the adjudication transition, records the decision and amount, and appends an immutable decision event.
known_pitfalls: payout without recorded amount or basis
decision events edited after the fact
duplicate approval from a retried request
success_signals: each decision recorded with amount and basis
decision events are append-only

blackbox.does: Tracks a contract across draft, review, signed, active, and expired states, recording effective and renewal dates and appending each status change for review.

problem_solution.problem: Contracts have legally significant states and dates, and a wrong or unrecorded transition can leave an expired contract treated as active or miss a renewal window.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent marks a contract active without capturing the effective and expiry dates, so renewal and expiry checks have nothing to key on.
problem_solution.solution: A contract-tracker capability that validates the lifecycle transition, records effective and renewal dates, and appends the status change.
success_signals: expiry and renewal dates present on active contracts
transitions follow the contract lifecycle

blackbox.does: Appends a typed, timestamped event to a customer's activity timeline with a deduplication key, so a unified chronological view of interactions can be read back.

problem_solution.problem: A unified customer timeline needs every interaction appended in order with a stable type, but events arriving from many sources duplicate and arrive out of order.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends events with no dedup key and trusts wall-clock order, so retried and out-of-order events create duplicate or scrambled timelines.
problem_solution.solution: A timeline-emit capability that appends a typed event with an event timestamp and a deduplication key, keeping the timeline ordered and duplicate-free.
known_pitfalls: ordering by ingest time instead of event time
untyped events breaking the timeline reader
success_signals: same event key appended once
timeline ordered by event time

blackbox.does: Applies a change to a customer's tracked profile and lifecycle stage, appending a state-change event so the customer's current status and its history stay in sync.

problem_solution.problem: A customer's current state and its change history drift apart when updates mutate the record without recording what changed and why.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites customer fields in place and logs nothing, so the lifecycle stage changes with no record of the transition.
problem_solution.solution: A tracker-update capability that validates the change, writes the new customer state, and appends a corresponding state-change event atomically.
success_signals: current state and latest event always agree
retried update yields one event

blackbox.does: Updates an employee's employment status, role, and department across the hire-to-exit lifecycle, appending each change to an access-controlled personnel history.

problem_solution.problem: Employee records hold sensitive personal data and drive access, so status, role, and department changes must be recorded and scoped to authorized viewers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent updates employment status but leaves downstream access unrecorded and exposes personal fields to unauthorized readers.
problem_solution.solution: An employee-tracker capability that validates the lifecycle transition, records role and department, and appends to a history readable only by authorized roles.
known_pitfalls: exposing personal fields to unauthorized viewers
termination not propagating to access state
success_signals: history readable only by authorized roles
termination reflected in employment status

blackbox.does: Applies a stock movement to an item's on-hand and reserved quantities under a non-negative constraint, recording the movement as an auditable ledger entry.

problem_solution.problem: Inventory quantities are updated concurrently from many sources, and unguarded writes cause lost updates, negative stock, or oversell of reserved units.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads a quantity, subtracts, and writes it back without a concurrency guard, so two simultaneous sales both succeed and stock goes negative.
problem_solution.solution: An inventory-tracker capability that applies each stock movement atomically under a non-negative constraint and records it as a ledger entry.
success_signals: concurrent movements apply without lost updates
on-hand never goes below zero

blackbox.does: Advances a sales lead through qualification and status changes, recording ownership, score, and stage transitions while appending the corresponding activity event.

problem_solution.problem: Leads move through qualification stages with ownership and scoring, and skipping or reordering those stages corrupts pipeline reporting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sets an arbitrary lead stage without checking the allowed transition, letting a lead jump backward or skip qualification.
problem_solution.solution: A lead-tracker capability that validates the stage transition, updates owner and score, and appends the activity event for the change.
success_signals: only allowed stage transitions applied
each change leaves one activity event

blackbox.does: Creates in-app notifications from events and updates their read, seen, and dismissed state per recipient, deduplicating repeat triggers into a single inbox item.

problem_solution.problem: A notification center must create items from events and track per-recipient read state, or the same event spams the inbox and read counts never settle.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts a new notification per trigger with no dedup and no read-state model, so the inbox floods and the unread badge is wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A notification-center capability that creates or coalesces items by dedup key and transitions read, seen, and dismissed state per recipient.
known_pitfalls: unread count drifting from actual state
one recipient's read state affecting another
success_signals: repeat triggers coalesce into one item
unread count matches per-recipient state

blackbox.does: Tracks completion of onboarding steps per user against a defined checklist, enforcing prerequisites and returning overall progress and the next actionable step.

problem_solution.problem: Onboarding checklists must mark steps complete against a defined set, honor prerequisites, and report progress, or steps complete out of order and progress is wrong.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent marks steps complete against a free-form list with no prerequisite check, so later steps complete before their required earlier ones.
problem_solution.solution: A checklist-state capability that validates steps against a defined checklist, enforces prerequisites, and computes progress and the next step.
known_pitfalls: progress miscomputed against a changed checklist
success_signals: prerequisites enforced before completion
progress and next step consistent with completed steps

blackbox.does: Moves an order through placed, paid, fulfilled, shipped, and returned states, recording the transition and the linked references that downstream fulfillment depends on.

problem_solution.problem: Order fulfillment depends on a strict status progression, and an out-of-order or duplicated transition can ship an unpaid order or fulfill twice.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent marks an order shipped without checking it was paid and fulfilled, letting an unpaid order leave the warehouse.
problem_solution.solution: An order-tracker capability that enforces the allowed status progression, records payment and fulfillment references, and appends each transition event.
known_pitfalls: duplicate fulfillment from a retried event
success_signals: only valid forward transitions applied
a retried transition does not fulfill twice

blackbox.does: Updates a project's status, milestones, and ownership, recording percent-complete and target dates and appending the change to the project's activity history.

problem_solution.problem: Project status, milestones, and dates change often, and updating them without a trail makes it impossible to explain how a project slipped.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the target date and status silently, so a slipped milestone shows no record of when or why it moved.
problem_solution.solution: A project-tracker capability that applies status and milestone changes, records dates and percent-complete, and appends the change to history.
success_signals: date and status changes appear in history
milestone state stays consistent with progress

blackbox.does: Scans tracked records for due reminders on a schedule, enqueues a reminder for each and marks it dispatched, so a due item is reminded once per due window.

problem_solution.problem: Scheduled reminder scans must fire each due reminder once, but overlapping runs and missing dispatch markers cause duplicate or missed reminders.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent selects due items and enqueues reminders without marking them dispatched, so the next run re-selects the same items and reminds again.
